Add schema-offered fields/operators with correctly typed numeric/Boolean/date/text/enum values. Sorting changes order, not filters. Paging continues the query without enlarging its period. For empty results remove filters one at a time and verify capture existed then.

sections.heading: Capture, retention, backup and Playback differ
sections.body: Capture decides admitted observations; retention decides storage duration; aggregation summarizes samples; backup preserves a recoverable copy. Capture fields are neither a global database quota nor archival configuration. Playback displays historical values in the current visualization, not process restoration or command authorization; return to live before operating. Missing samples mean neither zero nor stopped equipment.

en.title: Alarms: configure condition, priority and behavior
en.summary: Build an alarm from a TAG and understand what each option actually does.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: Open Engineering > Alarms. First verify the TAG reading, type, scaling and unit. A high-pressure alarm observes the TAG value; it neither configures the sensor nor stops the pump by itself. Agree on thresholds and operational response with the process owner. Learn with a simulation TAG without operating real equipment. Editing requires the applicable Engineering permission and lock.

sections.heading: Identity and condition
sections.body: Select New alarm or an existing definition. The path identifies the signal to evaluate; the name and message help operators understand the problem.

fields.label: Name
fields.description: Use a readable description distinguishing equipment and condition. Renaming does not change the observed TAG.

fields.label: TAG path
fields.description: Enter an existing TAG path. Check its already-scaled value in TAG Monitor before choosing the threshold.
fields.constraints: Not a Driver address or screen name.

fields.label: Type
fields.description: Selects the comparison rule; see the types below. HighHigh is another threshold definition, not automatic priority.

fields.label: Setpoint (threshold)
fields.description: Shown for analog types. Enter a number in the current TAG unit. High/HighHigh activate at value ≥ threshold; Low/LowLow at value ≤ threshold.
fields.constraints: Equality also activates. This editor has no hysteresis field.

fields.label: Active digital value
fields.description: Only shown for Digital. Checked means true is the alarm condition; unchecked means false. Verify actual signal polarity.

fields.label: Priority
fields.description: Orders and highlights attention: low, medium, high or critical. Does not change the threshold, permission or shutdown logic.

fields.label: Class
fields.description: Classification label for organizing definitions. Typing a name does not install a protection rule.

fields.label: Area
fields.description: Process context also used for area-scoped action authorization. Use the name expected by the policy; entering an area grants no access.

fields.label: Message
fields.description: Explain the condition and location usefully for the operator. A written instruction does not execute a command.

sections.heading: Choosing a type
sections.body: Digital compares the boolean with the selected active value. High and HighHigh use ≥; Low and LowLow use ≤. For two thresholds, create two definitions and choose their priorities separately. Communication activates for quality other than Good and returns with Good; it does not use a setpoint. With bad quality, process types do not evaluate the numeric limit as a valid reading: use a communication alarm to monitor this. System appears in the selector but has no generic process rule in this evaluator; do not use it instead of High or Digital. Selecting Communication does not imply a communication-loss timer.

sections.heading: Behavior and sound
sections.body: Expand Alarm behavior. Some options are saved in the definition but have current Runtime limitations, described alongside the field.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Includes the definition in evaluation when the revision is activated. Disabling fixes neither the signal nor the physical cause.

fields.label: Activation delay (ms)
fields.description: Represents the intended delay. Current limitation: the value is saved but does not delay Runtime activation. Do not rely on it to filter chatter.
fields.constraints: Integer field; delay not yet applied.

fields.label: Requires acknowledgement
fields.description: Expresses the intent to require operator ACK. Current limitation: clearing it does not remove pending acknowledgement in Runtime, including after return.

fields.label: Allow shelving
fields.description: Allows this definition to enter a suppressed state through an available operation. The action still requires AlarmShelve permission. The Alarm Center described here has no shelving button.
fields.constraints: Not Mute sounds; no automatic expiry is promised.

fields.label: Sound profile / preview
fields.description: Choose none, short pulse, double, triple, rising or alternating and try the preview. In Runtime, operators must enable sounds in the browser. Volume, output device and browser permission affect playback.
fields.constraints: Muting in the browser does not acknowledge the alarm.

sections.heading: Procedure: test a high threshold
sections.body: 1. Create a high alarm for the simulated pressure TAG with setpoint 10 and bar as the TAG unit. 2. Fill in priority, area and a clear message. Keep Requires acknowledgement checked for this test. 3. Run Preview, read errors and apply to Workspace. Any further edit requires validation again. 4. Save, publish and activate the correct revision; applying to Workspace alone does not activate Runtime. 5. With Good quality, send 9: the condition is Normal. Send 10: it becomes Active because equality reaches the threshold. 6. Acknowledge in Runtime: it becomes Acknowledged while the TAG remains 10. Send 9: it becomes Returned and leaves the active list because ACK was already recorded. 7. For another activation, send 10 then 9 without ACK: it becomes Returned pending acknowledgement. Acknowledge and verify removal from the active list. Use history for earlier transitions.

sections.heading: If the result differs
sections.body: Check the TAG/active revision, scaling/unit, boolean polarity, enablement and quality. High priority does not force activation. A chattering threshold gains no hysteresis from a different message or class. Preview validates a candidate; it does not prove field acquisition. Delay and ACK exemption retain the limitations described. If the project changes while editing, reload and validate again rather than applying an old candidate.

en.title: Runtime alarms: states, acknowledgement and sounds
en.summary: Read the current condition, acknowledge it and distinguish silence, return and history.

sections.heading: Where to look and how to interpret
sections.body: Open Runtime Alarm Center. It shows the active list visible to your session, counts and details for the selected item. It is not a list of all past occurrences. Select a row to inspect message/name, priority, area, last value, activation, last transition and who/when acknowledged. IDs in details identify the exact definition; you do not need to invent or type an ID to acknowledge.

sections.heading: States shown in details
sections.body: The active list includes Active, Acknowledged and Returned without ACK. An empty list therefore does not mean no alarm ever occurred. States outside it can be found through other appropriate queries.

fields.label: Normal
fields.description: Condition is not active now; a previous cycle may exist in history.

fields.label: Active
fields.description: Condition is present and this cycle is not yet acknowledged.

fields.label: Acknowledged
fields.description: ACK recorded but the condition remains present. It does not mean the cause was resolved.

fields.label: Returned
fields.description: Condition is no longer active. Without ACK it remains pending in the active list. After ACK it leaves that list.

fields.label: Disabled
fields.description: Definition disabled for evaluation. Does not indicate healthy equipment.

fields.label: Shelved
fields.description: Notification suppressed by shelving. Value and underlying state continue to be tracked; removing suppression restores the current underlying state.
fields.constraints: The current center provides no button for this action.

sections.heading: Procedure: acknowledge a notification
sections.body: 1. Select the row and read the condition, value and time; confirm the equipment. 2. Follow the plant operational response. 3. Use Acknowledge alarm if the session has AlarmAcknowledge permission for the area. A View Only session does not gain this action. 4. Wait for server confirmation and refresh. If ACK was accepted but refresh failed, refresh to verify the result before repeating actions. 5. If the condition persists, the acknowledged state remains visible. If it already returned, it leaves the active list after ACK. A new activation opens another pending acknowledgement.

sections.heading: Sounds, mute and unavailability
sections.body: Enable alarm sounds unlocks audio for this browser session, subject to support, volume and output device. Configured profiles repeat while an alarm awaits ACK, including Returned without ACK. Mute sounds is local and does not acknowledge, disable or shelve. Acknowledgement sends no process command. If access is denied, check login, session class and permission/area; do not try to fix access by changing the TAG. If data or service is unavailable, refresh and check Runtime diagnostics. For past transitions, open History and choose alarm.events with an appropriate period; do not confuse it with operational.events or Audit.

en.title: Operational events: define, emit and query
en.summary: Record a process occurrence with context, distinguishing definitions, occurrences, alarms and Audit.

sections.heading: Choose the right resource
sections.body: An operational event records a fact, such as batch start or mode change. Each emission creates an occurrence with its own time and identity; it maintains no active condition and requires no ACK. An alarm tracks a condition that activates/returns. Audit traces security/administrative actions and outcomes. A visual object click is also called an event but is not itself an operational occurrence. Creating the definition below emits nothing automatically; linking a TAG provides context, not a change trigger.

sections.heading: Definition fields
sections.body: Open Engineering > Operational Events and select New Operational Event. Define meaning and source first; expand Optional context when needed. Type/category/source labels are text from your convention, not connection settings.

fields.label: Display name
fields.description: Readable name for people.

fields.label: Key
fields.description: Text key unique across definitions, case insensitive. Not the stable ID used by the Python API.

fields.label: Type
fields.description: Describes the nature of the fact; does not select an alarm type.

fields.label: Category
fields.description: Groups occurrences using your convention for search and analysis.

fields.label: Source
fields.description: Semantically identifies what produces the fact. Entering server-script does not automatically create or bind a script.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Controls definition availability in the Runtime revision. Does not remove historical occurrences.

fields.label: Default message
fields.description: Text used if emission supplies no other message. An emission message may override it.

fields.label: Area (optional)
fields.description: Places the fact within the process organization; grants no user permission.

fields.label: Equipment path (optional)
fields.description: Equipment context reference. Does not create equipment or a drawing.

fields.label: TAG (optional)
fields.description: Choose an existing TAG; the editor stores its identity and path. No TAG is valid for a general fact.
fields.constraints: Association does not automatically monitor changes.

sections.heading: Procedure: prepare the definition and producer
sections.body: 1. Create the definition with required fields and useful context; avoid using one generic key for every fact. 2. Run Preview and read diagnostics. Fix duplicate keys and invalid references. 3. Apply to Workspace, then save, publish and activate using the project lifecycle. 4. Configure the producer: a Server Script can call emit_operational_event. Obtain the saved definition stable ID from exported project data/references; do not substitute the text Key. 5. Bind the Python handler to the appropriate Server trigger. Avoid Timer to record a single transition: every call creates another occurrence even with the same message. 6. Activate the revision containing both definition and script. 7. Produce a controlled fact and query operational.events in History with a period covering execution.

sections.heading: Python example: one occurrence at initialization
sections.body: The UUID below is illustrative: replace it with your definition stable ID. In Script Engineering choose Server scope and bind the Initialize event to the initialize handler; a function name alone does not create that binding. The example records simulation start at each script initialization, not a physical pump start. The event argument is trigger context and can remain unused. emit_operational_event(definition_id, message=None, context=None) returns None, not an occurrence ID. Context dictionary keys and values are strings: use str(value) for calculated numbers.

sections.heading: Query and troubleshoot
sections.body: In History select operational.events, set start/end and available filters; inspect time, source, message and context. alarm.events contains alarm transitions, while Audit has another purpose. Additional context does not change the definition's own type, category, source or identity, even with keys bearing those names. Context allows up to 128 pairs, keys up to 160 characters and values up to 4000; messages also have a 4000-character limit. Include no passwords or secrets. Missing occurrence: check active revision, enabled definition, correct ID, handler binding, script diagnostics, time range and query permission. Emission must respect active Runtime authority; failure does not authorize an alternative path. Nothing appearing after only creating a definition is expected.

en.title: Local users: create, assign roles and maintain access
en.summary: Register who signs in and distinguish account, role, session and license.

sections.heading: Before administering accounts
sections.body: Open Engineering > Security. Users and credentials belong to the installation Security Authority; they are not project objects and are not carried in the Engineering package. A local product account differs from a commercial portal account. User administration requires UserRoleAdmin or SystemAdmin; project editing alone does not grant it. Preserve at least one enabled local administrator and check which account you are using before changing roles or passwords.

sections.heading: Account fields
sections.body: Use New user to create an identity. For an existing account, select it in the list; its login name is shown for identification and is not renamed by this form. Password is entered during creation or in the separate reset form, without exposing the current password.

fields.label: Username / login
fields.description: Name used to sign in. Do not confuse it with the readable display name.

fields.label: Display name
fields.description: Identifies the person readably. Changing it changes neither login nor roles.

fields.label: Password / New password
fields.description: Create an individual password and follow the policy accepted by the server. Reset replaces the password rather than recovering the previous one. Never copy passwords into messages, scripts or packages.
fields.constraints: The form requires at least 8 characters; the server validates the policy.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Allows account use. Disabling deletes neither identity nor action history. Changes can invalidate the session; keep another administrative account available.

fields.label: Roles
fields.description: Select existing roles whose permissions match the work. Grants from assigned roles combine; adding a role removes no permission from another. Naming a role developer or administrator creates no privilege by itself.
fields.constraints: Check the grants, not just the name.

sections.heading: Procedure: create and test an operator
sections.body: 1. Inspect available roles and their capabilities/scopes in the Authority panel. If an appropriate role is missing, prepare and apply the policy first. 2. Select New user and enter login, name, private password and enablement. 3. Select only required roles and create the account. 4. For later changes, review the summary and confirm saving; editing fields alone does not save. 5. Sign in with the new account in a separate session and check a permitted read and an action that should be denied. License and View Only/Interactive class still restrict actions. 6. Return to the administrative account to correct grants if needed; do not use one session as evidence for two different users.

sections.heading: Reset, search and common problems
sections.body: Search filters name/login/role, and status separates enabled and disabled accounts; hiding a row does not disable an account. To reset a password, select the account, enter New password, review the impact and confirm. Account/role or password changes can end sessions; sign in again when requested. The system rejects removing the last enabled local administrative access and assigning nonexistent roles. A 401 calls for signing in again; 403 indicates insufficient permission. A project revision does not carry users, and importing .escadapkg does not restore Authority.

en.title: Roles and scopes: grant the action on the right resource
en.summary: Build explicit grants, check their reach and apply the validated Authority policy.

sections.heading: Account, role, capability and scope
sections.body: An account identifies the person. A role groups grants. Each grant pairs a capability, the permitted action, with an optional scope, where it applies. The policy belongs to Authority rather than a drawing or project package. Open Engineering > Security and the roles/capabilities/scopes panel. Reading policy requires UserRoleAdmin. Preview/apply requires EngineeringModify and either UserRoleAdmin or SystemAdmin. Role names grant no access by themselves.

sections.heading: Role and grant fields
sections.body: New role creates a draft. Duplicate copies settings into another role, not users. In the displayed hierarchy, IDs identify existing nodes/resources; this panel lets you select nodes but provides no form for creating or rearranging the hierarchy. Do not invent a UUID to replace a missing node.

fields.label: Stable identifier
fields.description: Key used in user assignments. Edit before first Apply. It is protected afterward; changing Display name does not change the key.

fields.label: Display name
fields.description: Readable label for selecting and recognizing the role. Not its permission list.

fields.label: Description
fields.description: Explain purpose and intended reach to prevent later mistakes.
fields.example: Read the station and acknowledge its alarms

fields.label: Capability
fields.description: Select the specific action. Use the reference below; similar names do not make capabilities interchangeable.

fields.label: Scope
fields.description: Unscoped grants this capability globally. Selecting a node restricts that grant to the corresponding resource. Global does not mean all capabilities.

fields.label: Include descendants
fields.description: With a selected node, includes its descendants in the authorization hierarchy. Unchecked covers only that node. It is not a name/path prefix search.

sections.heading: Available action reference
sections.body: These are the options shown in the current version. Permission creates no resource, changes no license and bypasses no active revision, readiness, context or operation limit.

fields.label: View
fields.description: View Runtime; grants no commands.

fields.label: TagRead
fields.description: Read TAGs for the authorized resource/scope.

fields.label: CommandExecute
fields.description: Execute registered commands. Distinct from writing a process value.

fields.label: ProcessValueWrite
fields.description: Request a process-value write, such as a setpoint. Does not replace command permission.

fields.label: AlarmAcknowledge
fields.description: Acknowledge alarms; does not fix the physical cause.

fields.label: AlarmShelve
fields.description: Shelve/unshelve alarms through an available operation, subject to the definition.

fields.label: TrendUse
fields.description: Use authorized queries/trends.

fields.label: TrendSave
fields.description: Save trend settings where available; grants no general project editing.

fields.label: EngineeringView
fields.description: Read authorized Engineering.

fields.label: EngineeringModify
fields.description: Modify Engineering subject to Engineering Lock and operation-specific requirements.

fields.label: UserRoleAdmin
fields.description: Administer users/roles through authorized flows. Policy mutation also requires Engineering editing.

fields.label: SystemAdmin
fields.description: Administer system operations requiring this capability, such as querying Audit. Do not assume it replaces every specific capability.

fields.label: HighAvailabilityObserve
fields.description: Observe HA status.

fields.label: HighAvailabilityTransfer
fields.description: Request HA authority transfer subject to readiness and permissions.

fields.label: HighAvailabilityAdmin
fields.description: Administer HA settings. An operation may require other Engineering permissions.

fields.label: AssetProcessIntelligenceManage
fields.description: Manage Intelligence with an explicit global grant or a valid Equipment/Location restriction. License and activation remain necessary.

sections.heading: Procedure: prepare and apply a policy
sections.body: 1. Load current policy and identify who will retain administration. 2. Create or select a role; check assigned users before editing. 3. Add a grant for each required capability and choose global or the appropriate node. Inspect reach before including descendants. 4. For Intelligence explicitly add AssetProcessIntelligenceManage: global or Equipment/Location with a valid resource link. Do not substitute SystemAdmin alone for this grant when configuring the tools. 5. Run policy Preview, correct errors and apply only the validated candidate. A new edit invalidates Preview. 6. Assign the role to the account and test allowed/denied access using that account. 7. If another administrator changed policy, reload and edit the current version. Do not apply an old version or delete users to bypass a conflict.

sections.heading: Preview, session and rejection
sections.body: Selected-user preview combines draft-role grants; it is explanatory and does not prove permission for a concrete resource. Effective capabilities belong to your current session, not the selected person. The backend decides each operation using identity, resource and scope; Runtime also considers session class and license. Authority policy uses its own versioned Preview/Apply: exporting a project does not activate it. Deleting an assigned role and losing the last administrator are rejected. If a node is missing or incompatible, select a correct link; do not broaden to global just to dismiss an error.

en.title: Audit: find actions and check recording health
en.summary: Use appropriate filters, read outcomes and distinguish an empty list from persistence failure.

sections.heading: What Audit answers
sections.body: Open Audit in the system. Access requires SystemAdmin in the authorized Runtime. Audit records protected actions and outcomes: who attempted which operation on which resource and when. Administrative success does not prove a pump physically started; inspect command feedback and TAGs. Audit does not replace alarm.events, operational.events or Historian readings. This screen queries/diagnoses and does not edit occurrences.

sections.heading: Query fields
sections.body: Leave optional filters empty to broaden the query. Filled filters combine: a record must satisfy all of them. Values are exact, not free-text fragments. Copy values from a known event instead of guessing IDs. Editing filters does not query until Query is selected.

fields.label: From
fields.description: Start in browser local time, converted to UTC for querying. Empty means no lower time bound.
fields.constraints: Must not be later than To.

fields.label: To
fields.description: End of period; the entered instant is included. If an event is missing, check timezone and period before assuming loss.

fields.label: User / subject
fields.description: Stable actor identity recorded in the event, not necessarily display name or login. Copy it from event details.

fields.label: Action
fields.description: Exact recorded operation name. Start with period/outcome if you do not know it.

fields.label: Outcome
fields.description: All leaves outcome unrestricted. Succeeded means recorded as successful; Denied is an authorization rejection; Failed is an unsuccessful operation.

fields.label: Resource kind (advanced)
fields.description: Target category, not the action name or TAG type.

fields.label: Resource / key (advanced)
fields.description: Exact target identifier used by the event. May be a key/path or ID depending on the operation; it is not always a UUID.

fields.label: Area (advanced)
fields.description: Area recorded in action context. A filter does not add an area to an event lacking one.

fields.label: Correlation ID (advanced)
fields.description: Links records from the same request/flow when correlation is provided. Not the individual event ID.

fields.label: Events per page
fields.description: Limits records shown on each page. Changes neither retention nor total stored records.

sections.heading: Procedure: investigate a denial
sections.body: 1. Choose a short period around the known attempt and Outcome = Denied. 2. Select Query. Select a row for details; keyboard and Enter also select. 3. Read identity, action, target and reason metadata; do not assume the license caused a denial. 4. Copy action/identity/target from details to refine filters if needed. 5. Check roles, grants and scope with Authority administration. Do not alter history to try granting access. 6. Use Next/Previous for pages with the same filter. Changing filters and selecting Query returns to page one. 7. Clear removes filters and queries again; it deletes no events. Refresh reloads the current page and diagnostics.

sections.heading: Diagnostics: read-only values
sections.body: Expand Diagnostics. A temporary queue does not prove loss, but failures/rejections/drops require investigation. Query health and recording health are different. These indicators are read-only: this screen has no retention policy editing fields.

fields.label: Persisted / last persisted
fields.description: Store count and last write time reported by the service; not just records on the current page.

fields.label: Append failures
fields.description: Indicates storage-write failures; inspect service diagnostics and database availability. A historical count does not prove a current failure.

fields.label: Pending queue
fields.description: Records awaiting buffer forwarding. Check whether the queue decreases after service recovery.

fields.label: Forwarded / forward failures
fields.description: Track buffer output and forwarding failures; distinct from query counts.

fields.label: Rejected by limit / dropped on shutdown
fields.description: Report records rejected by capacity or dropped during shutdown. Do not treat a queryable list as proof of completeness when these occur.

fields.label: Retention / last retention
fields.description: Shows enablement, finite/indefinite condition and execution of cleanup configured in the service. Indefinite means no active finite age, not unlimited disk. Backup and archiving are separate procedures.
fields.example: Inspect diagnostics; do not enter a value

sections.heading: No results or no access
sections.body: An empty list may mean no filter match, wrong period/timezone or absent recordings. Clear filters, check time and inspect diagnostics before concluding loss. A full page with no Next available does not prove no events exist outside the filter. A 401 calls for sign-in; 403 requires permission; 400 means an invalid filter. Pagination uses internal references supplied by the server: there is no cursor to enter in the form. This screen does not configure global database size or archiving; do not confuse retention diagnostics with that administration.

en.title: Engineering Lock: protect and reopen the application
en.summary: Use the application secret without confusing it with a user password, backup or permission.

sections.heading: When to use it and what it protects
sections.body: Engineering Lock protects application Engineering content. It is not another operator’s edit reservation and grants no capabilities to someone who knows the secret. An account password authenticates a person; the Lock secret protects the application; the Authority backup password protects different material. Store them appropriately rather than in screens, scripts or Help. When locked, system administration, Import/Export/Restore and unlock remain subject to their normal permissions.

sections.heading: States and actions
sections.body: In unlocked Engineering, open the padlock control in the top bar. When locked, the restricted surface presents the unlock form and available administration. Protected editors are not left open behind a simple message.

fields.label: Secret configured
fields.description: Indicates a secret exists. Configured does not necessarily mean currently locked.

fields.label: New secret / Replace secret
fields.description: Enter privately to configure or replace. The current secret is not displayed. Configure keeps Engineering open; Configure and lock closes protected Engineering.

fields.label: Lock now
fields.description: Uses the configured secret and switches to the restricted surface. Sends no stop command to Runtime.

fields.label: Engineering Lock secret / Unlock
fields.description: Enter the application secret to reopen content. Knowing a user password does not replace it; unlocking grants no missing permission.

fields.label: Remove secret
fields.description: Removes configured protection through the permitted flow. Neither resets a user password nor deletes the project.
fields.example: Only when protection removal is intended

sections.heading: Procedure and persistence after restart
sections.body: 1. With authorized access, open the padlock control. 2. Set the private secret and choose Configure to keep working or Configure and lock to restrict immediately. 3. Check the server-returned state. 4. Treat the change as Working state: Save → Publish → Activate is needed for the new protection to belong to the durable active revision after restart. Do not assume Configure alone completes that lifecycle. 5. To edit, use Unlock with the correct secret and appropriate permissions. 6. Check accessible content and preserve intended protection in the revision you publish. If rejected, read the reason; do not clear users, database or Authority to try unlocking.

en.title: Libraries: associate, inspect and incorporate resources
en.summary: Reuse resources without confusing the catalog with actual project content.

sections.heading: Choose the reuse mechanism
sections.body: Open Engineering > Libraries. An .escadalib file groups reusable resources such as Templates, Dynamos, Screens, Popups, Scripts and visual assets with dependencies. It is not a complete .escadapkg project, database backup or Authority. The catalog can show factory, project and associated-library origins. Association makes a library available for inspection; Use/incorporate copies the selected resource and required dependencies into Working. Only then is it project content. Visual Preview lets you inspect appearance without incorporation.

sections.heading: Fields, filters and information
sections.body: Name, type, category, origin and keywords help locate the right resource. No results may come from combined filters; clear them before importing another copy. Version/hash and dependency data are inspection information, not fields for arbitrary references.

fields.label: File to associate
fields.description: Select the received .escadalib. The server validates structure/content; renaming another file to this extension does not convert it.

fields.label: Origin / catalog filters
fields.description: Distinguish factory, project and associated library before use. Project resources already belong to Working; associated resources may still need incorporation.

fields.label: Dependencies / inspection
fields.description: Inspect resources accompanying the selection. A Screen may depend on Dynamos and images; incorporation can include more than one resource. Internal IDs/paths aid inspection, not manual recreation.

fields.label: New library name
fields.description: When exporting a selection, name the collection clearly. Not a Runtime application name.

fields.label: New library version
fields.description: Enter a version to identify the delivery. It describes the exported library; it neither changes project revision nor automatically updates incorporated copies.

fields.label: Resources to export
fields.description: Select existing project resources; choose the main item and inspect included dependencies. Export creates a file, not a published revision.

sections.heading: Procedure: use a received resource
sections.body: 1. Open Libraries and associate the file. Check name, version and origin. 2. Choose the library and filter the resource type. Inspect dependencies; use visual Preview when available. Association and Preview do not change Working. 3. Use/incorporate the desired resource; wait for confirmation and project refresh. This changes Working and may reuse equivalent content already present. 4. Open the resource in its appropriate area. Check TAGs, commands, parameters and references: a pump picture cannot infer your pump TAG. 5. Insert/configure objects in Screens or Popups and test. Save, publish and activate before checking Runtime. 6. To export your collection, enter name/version, select resources and download .escadalib. Reopen it in a test project to verify dependencies were included.

sections.heading: Updates, disassociation and failures
sections.body: Disassociate removes the library from the associated catalog; it does not delete incorporated project resources. Recorded origin is informational, not automatic synchronization with future versions. The same library ID with different content can conflict; check the required version before disassociating and associating another file. Unavailable Preview does not prove the whole package invalid: some kinds have no visual preview. If Workspace changed during the operation, reload before retrying. Association supplies no Driver credentials, users or license. The current associated catalog is process-local and may disappear after service restart; retain the file to associate it again. This differs from resources already incorporated and saved in the project.

en.title: Visual assets: import, name and use images
en.summary: Organize graphics files and preserve references when renaming.

sections.heading: Graphics file and visual object
sections.body: Open Engineering > Visual assets. An asset is the image/model file; a Screen object displays it. Importing an image creates no TAG, command, parameterized Dynamo or Screen instance. Factory catalog and project assets are shown separately. Dynamo artwork or factory content may not appear in the user-image list; check its origin before importing duplicates.

sections.heading: Fields and actions
sections.body: Use Preview to check content, then a readable name to find it in the editor. Types offered by the picker are still service-validated; changing extensions is insufficient.

fields.label: Import file
fields.description: Select PNG, JPG, BMP or SVG for images; the picker also accepts GLB/GLTF for supported models. Check that the target object supports the type; not every control renders 3D.

fields.label: Display name
fields.description: Initially taken from the filename without extension. Rename changes the label and preserves stable identity used by references.

fields.label: Delete / confirm
fields.description: Requires confirmation and may be rejected when the asset is in use. Remove or replace project references before trying again.

sections.heading: Procedure and verification
sections.body: 1. Import a file and wait for service confirmation. 2. Check Preview and name; adjust the label if needed. 3. Open the Screen/Popup and insert a compatible object, choosing the asset through its library/picker. For background or branding, use the relevant configuration field. 4. Adjust size/aspect ratio on the Screen; this does not alter original image pixels. 5. Save, publish and activate before checking Runtime. If missing, check reference, supported type, revision and content availability; do not replace an asset merely because another has the same-looking name.

en.title: TAG Gateway: configure and test a route
en.summary: Transfer values between server TAGs with explicit quality, conversion and diagnostics.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body: Open Engineering > Gateway. A route reads a source TAG and requests a destination TAG write through Runtime. It can connect already-configured protocol sources, but creates no Data Source, address or connection by itself. Transfer is one-way, not automatic two-way synchronization. Do not build a return-route loop without analyzing effects. Learn with two Server Memory TAGs disconnected from equipment.

sections.heading: Route identity and endpoints
sections.body: Pickers offer TAGs with enabled, server-owned sources. Client Memory belongs to a browser and cannot be a route endpoint. Simulation can be a source but not a destination. The destination must allow writes; source and destination must differ. IDs retain internal identity; paths help check meaning.

fields.label: Route identifier
fields.description: Key identifying the route in project and diagnostics. The current form keeps route name alongside this identifier; tabular Key and Name are separate columns.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Controls route participation in the activated revision. Does not fix a destination failure.

fields.label: Source TAG
fields.description: Select the value feeding the destination. Check type, quality and scaling in TAG Monitor.

fields.label: Destination TAG
fields.description: Select a writable TAG already configured for equipment or Server Memory. A route does not automatically change its write permission.

sections.heading: Trigger, startup and conversion
sections.body: GoodOnly is the current quality policy: a bad-quality value is not transferred as valid. Conditional fields depend on mode/conversion. Periods are milliseconds and do not change the Driver acquisition cycle.

fields.label: OnChange / Periodic
fields.description: OnChange reacts to acceptable updates with deadband/minimum interval. Periodic checks the current value at its period; it does not manufacture Good quality for a bad source.

fields.label: Initial transfer
fields.description: Synchronize uses the first acceptable value available at startup. Wait for next avoids initial synchronization and awaits the next transfer condition. Assess effects before using physical destinations.

fields.label: Deadband (OnChange)
fields.description: Absolute source-unit difference from the last successfully transferred source value. A smaller difference is skipped; equality with the deadband can proceed. Neither a percentage nor alarm deadband.

fields.label: Minimum interval (OnChange, ms)
fields.description: Limits attempt frequency in change mode. Fast updates may coalesce and the current value is reread before writing; not a guaranteed queue of every sample.

fields.label: Period (Periodic, ms)
fields.description: Periodic transfer interval. Do not combine with OnChange deadband/minimum interval in a file.

fields.label: Exact / CheckedNumeric
fields.description: Exact requires direct compatibility without gain/offset. CheckedNumeric explicitly transforms numerics and validates the target type. Overflow or a fractional value lost in an integer conversion fails; there is no silent truncation.

fields.label: Gain
fields.description: Multiplier in destination = source × gain + offset. Absent defaults to 1. Not the Driver scaling adjustment.

fields.label: Offset
fields.description: Added after gain; absent defaults to 0. Check target unit/range before publishing.

sections.heading: Procedure: 11 becomes 27 without real equipment
sections.body: 1. Create writable Server Memory TAGs Server.Source Int16 and Server.Destination Int32 with no physical destination. 2. Create copy-speed using these endpoints, OnChange, Wait for next, CheckedNumeric, gain 2 and offset 5. Leave deadband/minimum interval empty for this first test. 3. Preview configuration, fix errors and apply to Workspace. Save, publish and activate. 4. In the test environment update source to 11 with Good quality. Check 27 at destination: 11 × 2 + 5. 5. Inspect transfer diagnostics/last error; acceptance does not prove physical actuation. 6. Only then assess range, unit, quality, startup and rate before choosing real endpoints. Never use a route to bypass Authority, licensing or HA authority.

sections.heading: Equivalent CSV and diagnostics
sections.body: This CSV uses readable paths without IDs. Both TAGs and their source must exist before Preview/Apply. In Import/Export choose Gateway routes and CSV; the file does not create TAGs. Runtime diagnostics describe the active revision, not the draft. Waiting for source calls for checking source/quality; Degraded and last error call for conversion/range/destination checks. Skipped/coalesced counters do not automatically mean a defect: inspect mode and limits. Importing a route performs no transfer before the appropriate lifecycle.

en.title: CSV and Excel: export, edit and import while preserving references
en.summary: Prepare one entity table, validate the candidate and inspect creates/updates.

sections.heading: Choose the file
sections.body: In project Import/Export/Management use CSV/Excel for TAGs, Alarms, Data Sources, Gateway routes or Operational Events. Choose one entity per file. For Screens, Popups, Templates, scripts and composite dependencies use appropriate project/library mechanisms rather than invented columns. Engineering CSV/XLSX is neither historical-value export nor Authority/database backup. Start with an export from the current version to preserve column names and conventions.

sections.heading: Workflow controls
sections.body: File and entity/format/mode identify the candidate. Any change requires Preview again. The summary reports creates, updates, skips and errors; skipped does not mean applied.

fields.label: Entity
fields.description: Choose the object type contained in rows. A route spreadsheet cannot be read as TAGs.

fields.label: CSV / XLSX
fields.description: CSV uses commas and quotes text containing commas/quotes/newlines. XLSX accepts one sheet with the entity name used by export. Renaming old .xls does not create XLSX.

fields.label: Merge mode
fields.description: CreateOnly creates new and skips existing; UpdateExisting updates existing and skips new; CreateAndUpdate does both. Matching uses entity identity, not row position. This neither replaces everything nor deletes absent items.

fields.label: File and confirmation
fields.description: Select the saved file, Preview and read diagnostics before confirming Apply. Content must match what was validated; reload/revalidate if Workspace changes.

fields.label: Reference keys and paths
fields.description: Current exports use readable paths/keys and hide internal IDs. Preserve TAG path/entity key for updates; a new key may create another object. References must exist in the appropriate project/candidate.

sections.heading: Editing rules in Excel or text editors
sections.body: Keep exported technical headers even when the UI is translated. Unknown or duplicate columns can block import. Use decimal point (2.5) and booleans true/false; do not append units to numbers. JSON fields require valid JSON, not Python or semicolon lists. Preserve paths/keys as text to prevent automatic date/number conversion. XLSX formulas are rejected even with cached results: paste values before saving. The single sheet must be Tags, Alarms, DataSources, GatewayRoutes or OperationalEvents for the chosen entity. Include no users, password hashes, login credentials or secrets; protected Data Source references are not secrets themselves. Start complex fields from a real export, not a simplified example.

sections.heading: Example: two TAGs for the Gateway test
sections.body: A Server Memory source with key memory.server must exist. This minimal CSV creates the Gateway example TAGs, not the source. In a test project select TAGs/CSV and Preview, inspect both items and apply through the protected flow. Then import the route from the Gateway guide. A reduced-column table is for guided creation: preserve full exports when updating complete objects, because omitted columns may assume defaults rather than preserve previous values.

sections.heading: Complete procedure and error recovery
sections.body: 1. Export the current entity and keep a copy before editing. 2. Edit a small selection; preserve references/types. For expansion use unambiguous new paths/keys and create Data Sources before TAGs, then dependent alarms/routes/events. 3. Save values only in the chosen format and reselect the file. 4. Choose mode and Preview; inspect counts and error rows. Preview does not modify Working. 5. Confirm Apply of the validated candidate, then inspect objects in the editor. 6. Save, publish and activate to change Runtime through project lifecycle. 7. For row errors correct the file cause rather than deleting rows to hide dependencies; Preview again. If an update lost an option, compare omitted/defaulted columns with the original full file. Export is a configuration copy, not automatic activation rollback.

en.title: Data Source: from connection to a verified TAG
en.summary: Configure a connection before linking values to screens, alarms and history.

sections.heading: Before entering values
sections.body: In Engineering → Data Sources, have the address/node/topic map, network or serial settings and a known reading available. The SCADIVO server performs communication; browser access does not prove the server can reach the equipment. Start with one read-only TAG.

fields.label: Source key
fields.description: Identifies the connection in TAG references. Use a readable key distinct from other sources; this is not an IP address.

fields.label: Name
fields.description: Name shown in the list. Describe the equipment or service this connection serves.

fields.label: Connection type / driver
fields.description: Selects the protocol and its fields. Modbus TCP, Modbus RTU Master, MQTT Raw and OPC UA are different connections; changing type requires reviewing TAG bindings.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Includes the source in operational configuration when its revision is activated. Enabling does not repair the network, credentials or an incorrect TAG binding.

fields.label: Protected references
fields.description: Password/certificate fields take the reference to material provisioned on the server. Ask the administrator for the correct reference; do not paste the password, private key or certificate contents into ordinary configuration fields.

sections.heading: Prepare, check and activate
sections.body: 1. Create or select the source and choose the correct driver. 2. Fill basic fields and open advanced fields only when their defaults need changing. 3. Use Test connection where the driver offers it; a draft test does not apply changes. 4. Check changes and read diagnostics; Apply to Workspace updates working configuration. 5. Configure a TAG with this source, type and protocol binding; test its read where available. 6. Save/publish and activate the revision through the project workflow so Runtime uses this configuration. 7. Check value, unit, quality and updates before adding commands or alarms.

sections.heading: Connected but no value
sections.body: A connection test confirms its own step, not the whole map or a physical action. Check source enabled state, TAG binding, active revision and diagnostics. Access denied differs from timeout; bad quality differs from zero. ReadOnly and write permissions still apply even if a protocol supports writes. Discovery/testing features depend on the driver; MQTT Raw does not advertise an Engineering connection test.

en.title: Modbus: TCP, serial and register maps
en.summary: Prepare a TCP client or RTU master and understand each value address and representation.

sections.heading: Choose client or master
sections.body: Use Modbus TCP to query a network server/controller and Modbus RTU Master to query slaves on the host serial bus. This walkthrough does not configure SCADIVO as a Modbus Server; that type has a different role. Have the vendor map and start with a known variable without writes.

sections.heading: TCP connection and shared timings
sections.body: Host and port belong to TCP. Unit ID, scan, timeout and gap also apply to RTU, with its Unit ID limit.

fields.label: Controller host
fields.description: DNS name or IP reachable from the SCADIVO server running the driver. localhost means that server or container, not the browser computer.

fields.label: TCP port
fields.description: Port where the controller serves Modbus TCP. It is not the SCADIVO web or API port.

fields.label: Source Unit ID
fields.description: Logical device address; with a TCP/serial gateway it may select a slave. Applies to TAGs without an individual override. Use the equipment manual value, not the last part of its IP address.
fields.constraints: TCP: 0–255. RTU: 0–247. Default 1; the target must respond to reads.

fields.label: Scan interval (ms)
fields.description: Requested time between read cycles. 1000 ms is 1 second; reducing it increases traffic and load. Reducing this field cannot make a slow response faster.

fields.label: Response timeout (ms)
fields.description: How long to wait for a request. Unlike scan time, a short timeout may fail on a slow network/bus; a long timeout delays absence detection.

fields.label: Maximum address gap
fields.description: Advanced: combines nearby reads in one block, including the gap. Some controllers reject blocks crossing unimplemented addresses; reduce the gap in that case. It does not change TAG addresses.

sections.heading: Serial on Windows, Linux and Docker
sections.body: Use the actual equipment parameters. The host manages the bus; shared settings must be compatible. If the port cannot open, check the device, process/container permission and another program holding the port before changing TAG maps.

fields.label: Server serial port
fields.description: Device visible to the server/DriverHost: for example COM3 on Windows or /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux. In Docker the host must expose the device to the container and grant access. The browser serial port is not used; configuration can be prepared offline.

fields.label: Baud rate
fields.description: Must match devices on the same serial bus. A higher speed works only if the equipment and installation support it.

fields.label: Data bits
fields.description: Part of serial framing. Match the equipment; this is not the TAG numeric type size.

fields.label: Parity
fields.description: Serial frame check; all devices sharing the line need compatible configuration.
fields.constraints: None / Odd / Even / Mark / Space; default None.

fields.label: Stop bits
fields.description: Completes serial framing with baud, data bits and parity. Match the equipment.

sections.heading: TAG binding and conversion
sections.body: The address selects where to read; wire type selects interpretation. These are separate decisions. discrete/input are read-only; enabling TAG writes does not make the area writable. The TAG type must hold the conversion result.

fields.label: TAG area and address
fields.description: Use coil for Boolean output, discrete for Boolean input, holding for read/write register and input for input register. Canonical addresses start at zero: holding:0. If the vendor calls its first holding register 40001, confirm that convention before conversion; do not automatically enter 40001 as the offset.
fields.constraints: Offset 0–65535; the complete value must fit the area.

fields.label: Individual Unit ID
fields.description: Overrides the source Unit ID only for this TAG. Leave empty to inherit; for RTU also check slave/bus limits.

fields.label: Wire value type
fields.description: Defines interpretation of equipment bits. If omitted, inferred from the TAG type. Int16/UInt16 use 1 register, Int32/UInt32/Float32 use 2, Int64/UInt64/Float64 use 4; confirm the vendor map and compatibility with the TAG type.

fields.label: Word order
fields.description: Only affects values using several registers: HighWordFirst places the most significant word first, LowWordFirst the least significant. It is not byte order inside a word; do not change randomly to mask an incorrect address/type.

fields.label: Scale multiplier
fields.description: Converts the read value: displayed value = raw × scale + offset. For tenths of bar, 253 × 0.1 + 0 = 25.3 bar. Avoid applying the same conversion again in another layer.

fields.label: Offset
fields.description: Addition after scaling. Use only when the equipment map requires an origin correction.

sections.heading: Example and diagnosis by layer
sections.body: 1. Configure the TCP source with the actual host, port 502, controller Unit ID and initial 1000/3000 ms timings. 2. Create a read-only Double TAG, holding:0, wire type Int16 for a register representing tenths of bar. 3. Use scale 0.1, offset 0; if the known raw value is 253, expect 25.3 bar. 4. Test the read and check before activating the revision. Timeout calls for checking connectivity/Unit ID; illegal address calls for area/base; absurd values call for type/order/conversion. Do not use a write as a read test.

en.title: MQTT: topics, JSON and value freshness
en.summary: Connect to a broker and turn messages into typed values, separating subscriptions and publication.

sections.heading: A broker is not a sensor
sections.body: MQTT Raw receives messages when published. It does not poll like Modbus or automatically discover TAGs from arbitrary JSON. Have the host, port, TLS, authentication, topics and actual payload samples. Start with one read-only Double TAG.

sections.heading: Connection, session and resources
sections.body: Session fields differ between MQTT 3.1.1 and 5. Check the version before advanced settings. Size/queue limits bound memory use; they are not history storage.

fields.label: Broker host
fields.description: Server receiving/publishing messages, reachable from the SCADIVO server. It is not a topic or a URL path.

fields.label: Broker port
fields.description: Use the port actually configured on the broker; it must match TLS use.

fields.label: TLS connection
fields.description: Enables protected transport. Disabling does not automatically change the port or repair an invalid certificate. Match the broker mode and trust chain.

fields.label: MQTT client ID
fields.description: Identifies this connection to the broker. Choose a unique value per active client; reusing it in another connection can disconnect the previous session. It is not the login.

fields.label: MQTT version
fields.description: mqtt5 uses Clean Start and session expiry; mqtt311 uses Clean Session. Select the broker-supported version without mixing their options.

fields.label: Broker user name
fields.description: Account authorized by the broker for the topics in use; it is not the SCADIVO login.

fields.label: Broker password reference
fields.description: Protected reference resolved by the server. Without provisioned material or broker permission, authentication cannot succeed; do not enter a literal password instead of the reference.

fields.label: Keep Alive (seconds)
fields.description: Broker connection supervision interval; it does not request fresh measurements from a device.

fields.label: Connection timeout (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for a connection attempt, separate from TAG value freshness.

fields.label: Minimum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Minimum wait between attempts after losing connection. Coordinate with the maximum to avoid continuous attempts.

fields.label: Maximum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Caps the growing wait. Must be greater than or equal to the minimum.

fields.label: MQTT 3.1.1: Clean Session
fields.description: false requests session continuity on the broker with the same Client ID. true requests a clean session. Do not use this option in MQTT 5 mode.

fields.label: MQTT 5: Clean Start
fields.description: true starts without reusing the previous session; false requests continuity. It is separate from expiry time after disconnection.

fields.label: MQTT 5: session expiry (s)
fields.description: How long the broker keeps the session after disconnect. With Clean Start false it must exceed zero. It does not keep values forever fresh or replace history.

fields.label: Maximum message size (bytes)
fields.description: Memory limit per received payload; larger messages are rejected. Size for the actual document, not the number of TAGs.

fields.label: Consecutive connection failure limit
fields.description: Consecutive failure limit used by readiness supervision. Increasing it does not fix credentials or an unavailable broker.

fields.label: Maximum buffered messages
fields.description: Limits the transport message queue. A larger buffer consumes more memory; it is not archival or a promise to retain everything through an outage.

sections.heading: Read, quality and write
sections.body: Each TAG uses an exact topic and a type. One document can feed separate TAGs with different Pointers. QoS, retention and freshness serve different purposes; a value can exist and be Stale.

fields.label: Subscribe topic
fields.description: Exact topic feeding this TAG, preserving case. Do not use + or # as TAG identity; give separate topics/fields their own TAGs.

fields.label: Payload format
fields.description: utf8Scalar reads one textual value, such as 12.5 or true. json reads JSON and can extract a field with JSON Pointer. The result must match the TAG type.

fields.label: JSON value field
fields.description: JSON Pointer path, not Python or JSONPath: /current reads current at the root; /motor/current reads inside motor; /values/0 reads the first item. ~1 represents / in a name; ~0 represents ~. Empty selects the root, which must be a compatible scalar.

fields.label: Source timestamp field
fields.description: JSON field stating when the source measured the value. Use an explicit UTC Z timestamp in the example; measurement time differs from broker arrival.

fields.label: Require source timestamp
fields.description: With true, also configure the timestamp Pointer and publish a valid instant; otherwise the sample is rejected.

fields.label: Freshness timeout (ms)
fields.description: Optional: after this interval without a fresher sample the value becomes Stale. It does not request a publication from the device. Allow margin above the normal send period.

fields.label: Broker-retained value
fields.description: staleWithoutSourceTimestamp marks a retained value without source timestamp as Stale. acceptAsCurrent treats it as current; choose only if the application can assume that. A retained message does not prove the equipment is connected now.

fields.label: Subscribe QoS
fields.description: 0: at most one delivery; 1: at least one, possible duplicates; 2: exactly-once MQTT delivery within the session. QoS does not confirm physical actuation or sensor validity.

fields.label: Publish topic
fields.description: Required for a writable point and must be exact. Use the equipment command topic, separate from feedback where its contract requires. Do not accidentally publish to the measurement topic.

fields.label: Publish QoS
fields.description: Requested delivery quality when publishing, using the same 0/1/2 values. Broker acknowledgement is not process feedback.

fields.label: Retain publication
fields.description: false by default. true asks the broker to retain the last published payload; consider the risk of a new subscriber receiving an old command. Only applies to writable points.

sections.heading: Payload example: motor current
sections.body: Publish this example on plant/pump01/state on the test broker. For a Double TAG use json format, Pointer /current, timestamp /timestamp and required timestamp. Expected decoded value is 12.5. The instant is illustrative: in a live test use a current timestamp and check quality/age, not just the number. Do not paste this JSON as source configuration.

sections.heading: Publication limits and diagnosis
sections.body: Extracting /current for reads does not create a command-document template. JSON writes with a nonempty field Pointer are rejected: the product does not reconstruct an envelope. For writes use a scalar or root-JSON contract compatible with the equipment, a writable TAG, publish topic and authorization. If connected without values, check exact topic, publication, Pointer, type and timestamp. For Stale check retention, source time and freshness interval; do not mask missing measurements by accepting everything as current.

en.title: OPC UA: endpoints, certificates and node import
en.summary: Select the server, approve its identity and associate variables using the correct nodes.

sections.heading: Discovery is not activation
sections.body: In the OPC UA source use discovery to inspect offered endpoints and modes. Selecting a candidate fills parameters; it does not create protected credentials or automatically approve certificates. Engineering tests/browsing are temporary and do not change the active revision.

sections.heading: Connection and identities
sections.body: Secure channel and user authentication are separate settings. The client must be accepted by the server, and SCADIVO must recognize the approved server. Ask the administrator for provisioning and references; the Engineering file must not become a secret store.

fields.label: OPC UA server endpoint
fields.description: Complete opc.tcp URL reachable from the SCADIVO server. Discover endpoints and select one the server actually offers.

fields.label: Security mode
fields.description: None leaves the channel unprotected; Sign signs; SignAndEncrypt signs and encrypts. The mode must exist on the selected endpoint and match the policy; do not downgrade just to hide a certificate failure.

fields.label: Security policy URI
fields.description: Use the complete URI supplied by the endpoint, not only its short name. None requires a policy ending in #None; a secured mode cannot use that policy.

fields.label: Approved ApplicationUri
fields.description: Server application identity when pinned. This is not the connection address. Compare with the administrator-approved identity.

fields.label: Approved certificate SHA-256
fields.description: Secured Runtime requires explicit approval of the server certificate. Verify its fingerprint through a known channel before recording it; a changed certificate requires another check. This is not a private key.

fields.label: OPC UA server authentication
fields.description: Anonymous, UserName or Certificate as permitted by the server. Anonymous does not remove channel protection; this is separate from SCADIVO login.

fields.label: OPC UA user name
fields.description: Fill in UserName mode using an account authorized on the source server.

fields.label: OPC UA password reference
fields.description: In UserName mode, protected reference to the password provisioned on the host; not the plaintext password.

fields.label: Client certificate reference
fields.description: Client application identity for a secured channel. Must be provisioned on the host and accepted by the server. Do not confuse with the user certificate.

fields.label: User certificate reference
fields.description: In Certificate mode identifies the user separately from the client application certificate. The administrator supplies the protected reference.

fields.label: Session timeout
fields.description: Requested session duration; not a sampling interval. Format hours:minutes:seconds.

fields.label: Publishing interval
fields.description: Requested notification delivery pace for the subscription. Separate from each node sampling interval; the server can negotiate supported values.

fields.label: Temporary Engineering trust
fields.description: For a temporary Engineering session only. Does not approve the Runtime certificate: activation with auto-trust is rejected. After inspection record the approved identity and leave this option disabled in operational configuration.

sections.heading: Browse and bind TAGs
sections.body: In the OPC UA browser select suitable variables, check type/access and review the import preview. Apply the candidate only after checking conflicts. The binding stores node identity; renaming the TAG should not mean selecting another node.

fields.label: NodeId
fields.description: Server node identifier; for example ns=2;s=Pump.Current. It is neither the display name nor the SCADIVO TAG path. Prefer selecting it in the OPC UA browser to avoid typing errors.

fields.label: Namespace URI
fields.description: Stable namespace identity. When available it identifies the same node even if its ns= index changes. Use the server URI; do not invent one from the equipment name.

fields.label: Sampling interval
fields.description: Requested pace for observing this node. Format hours:minutes:seconds; choose a frequency suitable for the process and check server-negotiated behavior.

fields.label: Node queue size
fields.description: Number of samples the item queue can retain between deliveries. Larger uses more resources; it does not replace Historian.

fields.label: Discard oldest
fields.description: When the queue fills, true favors new samples; false requests preserving older samples rather than replacing the oldest. Check the server queue policy.

sections.heading: Identity example, not an import file
sections.body: This example shows two binding fields: NodeId ns=2;s=Pump.Current and namespaceUri urn:example:plant. Replace with your server values or use the browser. If its namespace index changes from 2 to 4 with the same URI and s=Pump.Current identifier, the stable identity remains the same. Do not use the sample name to guess an existing node.

sections.heading: Verify and troubleshoot
sections.body: 1. Discover and select compatible endpoint/mode/policy. 2. Verify server identity/certificate and provision client material for its authentication. 3. Test connection and browse to a known variable. 4. Review/apply import of at least one TAG and check the read. 5. Remove temporary trust and confirm approved Runtime configuration. 6. Save/publish/activate through the project workflow and check quality/timestamps. Rejected certificates require trust/identity checks; missing nodes require NodeId/namespace checks; denied access requires account/permission checks; incompatible types require TAG review. Accepted writes do not prove actuation: check equipment feedback.

en.title: Home/Building: incorporate a device
en.summary: Turn discovery into Equipment, TAGs and commands while checking what will actually be created.

sections.heading: Source, device and Location differ
sections.body: A Data Source stores communication settings; Equipment represents the device; Location organizes where it is. Functional capabilities such as OnOff, Temperature or Cover describe equipment functions, not Authority permissions. Discovering/incorporating a device does not automatically authorize commands.

fields.label: Integration source
fields.description: Source already configured in Data Sources. Its type must offer discovery to appear in this workflow; an empty list does not prove the entire network is empty.

fields.label: Discovered device
fields.description: Select a candidate and inspect TAGs, commands, capabilities and warnings. Discovered does not mean incorporated; this form cannot incorporate candidates without materialization.

fields.label: Device name
fields.description: Readable name for the Equipment to create. Does not rename the physical device or its source identity.

fields.label: Device path
fields.description: Organizes Equipment in the project. Check conflicts in preview; it is not an IP, NodeId or topic.

fields.label: Location
fields.description: Optional: select an existing Location for the device. Create Locations in their area before association. This does not grant access permission.

sections.heading: From discovery to active revision
sections.body: 1. Configure and apply the source in Engineering → Data Sources with protected material available on the server. 2. Open Home/Building → Devices, select the source and discover candidates where supported. 3. Choose a device and read warnings plus TAG/command/capability lists. 4. Set name, path and Location and check preview; configuration has not changed yet. 5. Apply only a valid preview; if Workspace changes, generate a new preview before applying. 6. Save/publish/activate through the project workflow and check state, quality, unit and authorized commands.

sections.heading: No candidate or missing function
sections.body: Check saved source, server-side connectivity and driver-advertised features. KNX/IP Secure advertises no Engineering discovery; Home Assistant has the selection limitation in its guide. An unmapped function is not delivered: inspect warnings and actual generated fields. A gateway/bridge can expose a device without SCADIVO having its native protocol. Do not repeatedly import to repair network or permissions.

en.title: BACnet/IP: device, objects and properties
en.summary: Configure the UDP network and select object identity; names and network addresses do not replace the binding.

sections.heading: Before connecting
sections.body: This driver is BACnet/IP over UDP; it does not advertise BACnet Secure Connect. Have device instance, route/IP/port and server-side network access. In Docker check networking and UDP; broadcast discovery depends on topology, not the browser. Start with a known read-only object.

sections.heading: Connection and binding fields
sections.body: Binding identity contains device, object type/instance and property with optional index. COV and priority configuration do not change that identity.

fields.label: Device instance
fields.description: BACnet device identity, not its IP or an object instance. The TAG binding device instance must match the source. Check it on the controller or through discovery.

fields.label: Manual target address
fields.description: Optional: device IPv4 with UDP port. Useful for a known target; does not replace deviceInstance identity.

fields.label: Local UDP port
fields.description: Port where the SCADIVO process listens for BACnet/IP. Another application/container may already use it; check firewall and UDP exposure on the server.

fields.label: Polling interval (ms)
fields.description: Requested polling pace for polled points. It is not a guaranteed COV-event frequency.

fields.label: BACnet timeout (ms)
fields.description: Wait for a BACnet request. Separate from discovery window and polling interval.

fields.label: Discovery window (ms)
fields.description: How long to collect discovery responses. Increasing may help a slow network but does not make broadcasts cross a blocked subnet.

fields.label: BBMD address
fields.description: Optional: administrator-configured BACnet distribution point for the network scenario. Do not invent a BBMD for a simple local network.

fields.label: Foreign Device registration lifetime (s)
fields.description: Optional: registration duration at the BBMD. Requires bbmdAddress; not TAG freshness or history retention.

fields.label: Object type
fields.description: Numeric BACnet object code. In the example, 0 identifies Analog Input; use the browser/vendor map type, not the TAG Double type.

fields.label: Object instance
fields.description: Object number within the device. Analog Input 37 differs from another object type with instance 37.

fields.label: Property
fields.description: Code of the property to read. Example 85 is Present Value. Name, description and value are different properties; prefer browser selection to avoid incorrect codes.

fields.label: Array index
fields.description: Fill only for an array property when a specific element is needed. Empty preserves the whole property; do not add an index to a scalar value.

fields.label: Use COV when available
fields.description: Requests change notifications rather than relying solely on polling. Depends on the server/object and the driver retains read checks; no change does not imply lost connection.

fields.label: BACnet write priority
fields.description: Optional for a writable object accepting priority. Not an alarm priority or SCADIVO permission. An accepted write may not change the effective value if another command takes precedence; check feedback and equipment policy.

sections.heading: Example: analog input value
sections.body: The example identifies Present Value of Analog Input 37 on device 1201. It describes a binding, not a complete import package. Use discovery/browse and check type/unit before activation; replace identities with those of your equipment.

sections.heading: Verification and diagnosis
sections.body: Test connection, discover/browse objects and review preview before applying; activate through the project workflow. No response: check UDP, instance, target and topology/BBMD. Found object but invalid value: check property, index and type. Unsupported COV calls for reviewing notifications and read checks; lack of change is not zero. Rejected writes require checking access, writable object and priority as well as SCADIVO authorization.

en.title: KNX/IP Secure: tunnel, DPT and confirmed state
en.summary: Use KNX project addresses and keep commands separate from feedback.

sections.heading: Requirements and scope
sections.body: The implementation uses a managed XKNX sidecar for KNX IP Secure TCP tunneling and Data Secure. Installation needs its compatible runtime for Windows or Linux x64 and protected host material; a container needs those resources too. This type does not promise unsecured IP tunneling, multicast routing or automatic Engineering discovery. Obtain settings/addresses from the KNX project/administrator.

sections.heading: Gateway and point fields
sections.body:
The generic TAG assistant still produces a binding incompatible with the KNX/IP contract. UI authoring correction is pending; the fields below explain the contract, but there is no validated walkthrough to complete this binding with the current assistant. Do not attempt to fix it by changing DPTs or disabling security.

Configure the source and binding using the actual DPT. Passwords/keyring are protected references, not secret files inside the application.

fields.label: KNX gateway host
fields.description: IP/name of the KNX/IP Secure gateway reachable from the SCADIVO server. Not a group or individual address.

fields.label: Secure tunnel port
fields.description: Port of the Secure TCP endpoint configured on the gateway. Do not assume an unsecured IP tunneling gateway offers this service.

fields.label: Individual address
fields.description: Assigned KNX client address in area.line.device notation. Obtain from the KNX project/administrator to avoid duplication.

fields.label: Secure tunnel user ID
fields.description: Gateway Secure user ID, not a SCADIVO login. Must match the provisioned authentication material.

fields.label: Secure password reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the server for this integration. Ask the administrator for the reference; do not paste a password, token or secret key into ordinary settings or the application manual.

fields.label: Device authentication reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the server for this integration. Ask the administrator for the reference; do not paste a password, token or secret key into ordinary settings or the application manual.

fields.label: Data Secure keyring reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the server for this integration. Ask the administrator for the reference; do not paste a password, token or secret key into ordinary settings or the application manual.

fields.label: Command group / binding address
fields.description: Address in main/middle/subgroup notation for writes. In the portable binding this is the TAG Address; for a read-only TAG check the KNX project mapping. The generic TAG assistant still produces a binding incompatible with the KNX/IP contract. UI authoring correction is pending; the fields below explain the contract, but there is no validated walkthrough to complete this binding with the current assistant. Do not attempt to fix it by changing DPTs or disabling security.

fields.label: Authoritative state group
fields.description: Feedback source. For a writable TAG it must differ from the command group; the driver does not treat sending a command as confirmed state.

fields.label: KNX datapoint type (DPT)
fields.description: Defines telegram interpretation. 1.001/1.002 use Boolean TAGs; 5.001 and 9.001/9.004/9.007/9.024 use Float or Double in this driver. The example uses 9.001 for temperature. Do not choose DPT solely by apparent value size.

sections.heading: Example: separate command and return
sections.body: The example describes a Double TAG, DPT 9.001, with command group 1/2/3 and state group 1/2/4. Replace with groups existing in the KNX project. This is not an import package and contains no security material. Equal groups are rejected for writable points; feedback must exist on the device.

sections.heading: Verify in stages
sections.body: Check sidecar availability and protected references first, then host/port/user/individual address and groups/DPT/TAG type. Authoring with the current assistant requires the correction noted above. With a correctly validated binding, save/publish/activate through the project and check feedback before writing. Accepted sending without feedback must not artificially update state. This driver advertises no Engineering discovery.

en.title: Home Assistant Bridge: connect and select entities
en.summary: One source connects to a user-managed Home Assistant; only selected entities enter the project.

sections.heading: Local bridge with explicit identity
