sections.body: HAB means Home Assistant Bridge; HA in SCADIVO still means High Availability. Use Home Assistant reachable from the server and an authorized token provisioned as protected material. The integration does not manage Home Assistant accounts, copy its internal database or turn all its integrations into native SCADIVO drivers.

sections.heading: Connection, identity and current selection limit
sections.body: Connection testing verifies transport/authentication, not incorporation. In the current version the generic discovery page does not supply entity selection; empty selection does not necessarily mean network failure. For a known TAG, configure its source/binding explicitly in the TAG editor and check the read before activation. There is no automatic whole-instance import.

fields.label: Home Assistant host
fields.description: DNS name or IP reachable from the SCADIVO server. Use the source device or service without a URL path; localhost means the server/container, not the browser.

fields.label: Port
fields.description: Source service port, separate from SCADIVO UI/API ports. When changing TLS also check the actual service port.

fields.label: Use TLS
fields.description: Protects transport where the service offers TLS. Does not install certificates or automatically change the port.

fields.label: Base path
fields.description: Optional path prefix when Home Assistant is exposed through a proxy. The client appends /api/websocket. With no prefix leave empty; do not repeat the complete endpoint.

fields.label: Home Assistant token reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the server for this integration. Ask the administrator for the reference; do not paste a password, token or secret key into ordinary settings or the application manual.

fields.label: Connection timeout (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for establishing the WebSocket connection. Separate from each request timeout.

fields.label: Response timeout (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for a request response; neither the measurement period nor proof of physical actuation. A value that is too small can reject a slow source.

fields.label: Minimum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Minimum wait after connection loss; avoid continuous attempts. It does not repair rejected authentication.

fields.label: Maximum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Limit on increasing wait; must be greater than or equal to the minimum.

fields.label: Entity and field
fields.description: Use the exact entity and field: entity:sensor.temperature:state for state; entity:light.room:attribute:brightness for an attribute. A display name is not entity_id. Renaming entity_id in Home Assistant requires reviewing the binding.

fields.label: Entity selection for incorporation
fields.description: The driver requires explicit selection, but this version of the Home/Building page does not yet let you choose entities. Discovery can return an empty selection with no device to incorporate even with a valid connection. There is no ready selector on that page; the correction is pending.

sections.heading: Address examples
sections.body: Use state for entity state and attribute for an existing attribute. The example shows a sensor read and light brightness; not an import file. Check type/unit: numeric readings are not display text, and brightness commands use the driver-supported conversion. Renaming the source entity requires reviewing bindings.

sections.heading: Commands and unavailability
sections.body: Support is limited to implemented bindings: switch/light state, light brightness/color and cover position as supported by equipment. This form does not offer arbitrary calls to every Home Assistant service. unknown and unavailable are not zero or off. After commands check authoritative state; request success does not prove physical actuation.

en.title: ESPHome: native API, entities and deep sleep
en.summary: Connect directly to the device and incorporate only functions the driver maps.

sections.heading: What must be available
sections.body: Firmware must offer the ESPHome Native API. The driver connects on the local network without requiring Home Assistant, ESPHome Dashboard or a Python sidecar. In Noise mode the API key must be provisioned on the server; the browser does not connect directly to the microcontroller.

sections.heading: Connection and binding
sections.body: Prepare the source, test connection and use discovery to obtain actual entity keys. Advanced fields do not repair a disabled API or incompatible key.

fields.label: ESPHome host
fields.description: DNS name or IP reachable from the SCADIVO server. Use the source device or service without a URL path; localhost means the server/container, not the browser.

fields.label: Port
fields.description: Source service port, separate from SCADIVO UI/API ports. When changing TLS also check the actual service port.

fields.label: API encryption
fields.description: noise is preferred with a provisioned key. plaintext is an explicit compatibility option on a trusted network and must match firmware. Do not confuse the Noise key with a Wi-Fi password.

fields.label: Noise key reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the server for this integration. Ask the administrator for the reference; do not paste a password, token or secret key into ordinary settings or the application manual.

fields.label: Response timeout (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for a request response; neither the measurement period nor proof of physical actuation. A value that is too small can reject a slow source.

fields.label: Write reconciliation timeout (ms)
fields.description: How long to wait for authoritative state after a command. Accepted sending is not feedback; increasing the deadline does not guarantee movement/actuation.

fields.label: Minimum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Minimum wait after connection loss; avoid continuous attempts. It does not repair rejected authentication.

fields.label: Maximum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Limit on increasing wait; must be greater than or equal to the minimum.

fields.label: Keep Alive (ms)
fields.description: Connection supervision interval; does not increase sensor measurement frequency.

fields.label: Deep-sleep policy
fields.description: normal for continuously running devices; expected only for intentionally sleeping nodes. Changes reconnect defaults: minimum 500→10000 ms, maximum 30000→60000 ms. Absence remains unavailable, never healthy.

fields.label: Entity address
fields.description: Format kind:device-id:hex-key.field. Discovery supplies the 8-digit hexadecimal key; do not use the display name as a key. Example switch:0:00000010.state.

fields.label: Write kind
fields.description: Defines a supported entity write, not an arbitrary service: switchstate, lightstate, lightbrightness, coverposition, fanstate, fanspeedlevel, numberstate or selectstate. Prefer the discovery-generated binding. Entity/value type and ReadOnly remain checked.

sections.heading: Entity example
sections.body: This address represents state of a Switch entity, device-id 0, hexadecimal key 00000010. Use the key returned by your device; do not invent IDs. A writable Boolean TAG requires the compatible write kind. This is not an import package.

sections.heading: Function map and diagnosis
sections.body: Materialization includes supported process entities such as sensor, binary sensor, switch, light, cover, fan, number and select. Configuration/diagnostic entities and unmapped functions can be omitted with warnings; finding climate, lock or button in inventory does not imply full control of them. Check API, mode/key and connection first, then address/type and discovery warnings. For a sleeping node expected adjusts the connection cycle but still shows absence as unavailable.

en.title: Shelly Gen2+: components, measurements and commands
en.summary: Use local RPC and review channels/fields actually offered by the device.

sections.heading: Local connection with a compatible generation
sections.body: This driver uses Shelly Gen2+ RPC over HTTP/WebSocket; it is not a cloud API and does not promise compatibility with every Gen1 device. Have local host, port and device authentication. A component represents a device channel/function, not a SCADIVO user or Location.

sections.heading: Source and TAG fields
sections.body: Test connection and discover the device to obtain actual components. Preview shows only mapped measurements/commands; a friendly name does not replace the component key.

fields.label: Shelly host
fields.description: DNS name or IP reachable from the SCADIVO server. Use the source device or service without a URL path; localhost means the server/container, not the browser.

fields.label: Port
fields.description: Source service port, separate from SCADIVO UI/API ports. When changing TLS also check the actual service port.

fields.label: Use TLS
fields.description: Protects transport where the service offers TLS. Does not install certificates or automatically change the port.

fields.label: Device user
fields.description: Shelly RPC authentication account; default admin. Neither the SCADIVO user nor a Shelly cloud account.

fields.label: Shelly password reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the server for this integration. Ask the administrator for the reference; do not paste a password, token or secret key into ordinary settings or the application manual.

fields.label: Response timeout (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for a request response; neither the measurement period nor proof of physical actuation. A value that is too small can reject a slow source.

fields.label: Minimum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Minimum wait after connection loss; avoid continuous attempts. It does not repair rejected authentication.

fields.label: Maximum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Limit on increasing wait; must be greater than or equal to the minimum.

fields.label: Component and field
fields.description: Format component.field, for example switch:0.output or switch:0.aenergy.total. The number identifies the channel; do not use the friendly name as an address.

fields.label: Write RPC method
fields.description: For a writable binding, method supported by the equipment and driver; in the example Switch.Set. Prefer the discovery-generated binding without assuming every method can become a command.

fields.label: Write RPC parameter
fields.description: Field receiving the write value; Switch.Set uses on for the Boolean. Requires a writable TAG, compatible method and authorization. Confirmed state is read separately.

sections.heading: Example: output of channel zero
sections.body: The example binds switch:0 output to a Boolean TAG; the compatible write uses Switch.Set with parameter on. Check the actual channel before creating commands. JSON illustrates the binding; it is neither a direct request nor an import package.

sections.heading: Check measurements and feedback
sections.body: Fields depend on model: for example output, apower power, voltage, current and aenergy.total when present. The driver also maps bounded light/cover functions and supported sensors. A missing field is not a zero reading; inspect warnings and type/unit. For writes check response and confirmed state separately. For authentication failures check the protected reference and device account rather than switching to cloud credentials.

en.title: Zigbee and Z-Wave: choose the connection path
en.summary: Check who owns the network and which source type represents the installation.

sections.heading: Before filling fields
sections.body: This is a checklist, not a new configuration page. Source choice depends on the actual coordinator/controller and external installation. A radio must not be opened simultaneously by SCADIVO and another process controlling the same port.

fields.label: Connection path
fields.description: Native Zigbee uses the supported TI coordinator on the SCADIVO host. Zigbee2MQTT Bridge uses an external Zigbee2MQTT installation and its broker. Z-Wave JS Controller uses a prepared serial Z-Wave controller on the host. They are not interchangeable options for one device.

fields.label: Prepared network and devices
fields.description: Have the network and devices already commissioned through the coordinator/installation procedure. Engineering discovery queries what exists; it does not open inclusion, reset devices or create a network.

fields.label: Received value and confirmation
fields.description: A discovered device may not have every function mapped. Old state, transport acknowledgement and fresh feedback differ. Check quality and updates before using a TAG in a command, alarm or screen.

sections.heading: Physical network, TAG and UI have separate steps
sections.body: 1. Identify whether the network uses a supported local coordinator, external Zigbee2MQTT or local Z-Wave controller. 2. Confirm prepared network/devices, server access and protected material without accidentally creating another network. 3. Configure the matching source and check its specific authoring/selection limits. 4. With a valid binding check TAG, type, quality and feedback; save/publish/activate through the project workflow. 5. Add screens, alarms and authorized commands only after verifying a known reading.

en.title: Native Zigbee: coordinator and On/Off state
en.summary: Prepare the source for the supported TI coordinator and understand this version’s bounded scope.

sections.heading: Required installation
sections.body: This driver uses a TI zStack/CC2652 serial coordinator and distribution-managed helper process for Windows or Linux x64. In a container the host must expose the physical resource and persistent state. Network/device must already be prepared; this type has no Engineering discovery or inclusion wizard. It does not promise every Zigbee device/cluster.

sections.heading: Fields and authoring limit
sections.body: Network parameters must match the existing coordinator/state. Binding authoring in the generic assistant is incomplete: Runtime rejects its extra fields. The fields below describe driver requirements; the current assistant does not provide a corrected creation workflow.

fields.label: Host coordinator resource
fields.description: ID of an available serial physical resource registered by the installation as ZigbeeCoordinator, TI zStack family and CC2652 model. It is not a COM/tty path entered here. Ask the administrator for its ID and device access on Windows/Linux/container.

fields.label: Network identity
fields.description: Identity of the prepared network, which must match the evidence registered on the coordinator resource. Does not rename the physical network or replace PAN ID/key.

fields.label: PAN ID
fields.description: Existing network identifier. Use the installation value; prefer decimal in the numeric field. Changing it is not a repair procedure.

fields.label: Extended PAN ID
fields.description: Network identity with 16 hexadecimal digits matching the prepared coordinator. Not an actuator IEEE address or secret key.

fields.label: Network channel
fields.description: Zigbee channel used by the existing network. Changing only this project number does not safely migrate every device.

fields.label: Serial baud rate
fields.description: Coordinator serial link speed matching its firmware. Not measurement frequency or radio channel.

fields.label: Network key reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the host for this network. The administrator supplies the reference/slot; do not paste the secret key or put it in an Engineering package. Do not replace an existing key with a new value to troubleshoot connectivity.

fields.label: Device IEEE address
fields.description: 16-hex-digit identity of the already commissioned device. A friendly name or short network address does not replace IEEE.

fields.label: Endpoint
fields.description: Function endpoint on the device from its actual mapping. Not a TCP port or dashboard channel number.

fields.label: Supported cluster
fields.description: This native driver accepts genOnOff in this version; it does not offer every Zigbee cluster or analog measurement through this binding.

fields.label: Supported attribute
fields.description: onOff attribute with a Boolean TAG. A different attribute or numeric TAG type is rejected.

fields.label: Complete TAG address
fields.description: Combines IEEE/endpoint/cluster/attribute. The example is an On/Off function; replace with the existing device identity.

fields.label: Binding authoring in this version
fields.description: The current generic assistant stores identity fields as extra settings, but this driver requires them only in the address. Runtime rejects the generated object. UI authoring awaits correction; do not bypass validation.

sections.heading: Example of a prepared function
sections.body: The example describes an existing Boolean function identity. It is not an import package and does not open inclusion. The driver binding stores identity in the complete address without duplicate extra settings. ReadOnly still controls write eligibility alongside Authority authorization.

sections.heading: Diagnosis and network preservation
sections.body: Check available resource, model/family, serial access and network identity before reviewing TAGs. Then check IEEE/endpoint and Boolean/genOnOff/onOff. Do not repair failures by deleting persistent state, changing keys or creating another network without the appropriate maintenance procedure. A write followed by a read checks state, not physical actuation.

en.title: Z-Wave JS Controller: prepared network and persistent values
en.summary: Use the host-registered controller and preserve each value’s exact identity.

sections.heading: What this type does
sections.body: The managed helper uses a local serial controller and internal communication restricted to the host. Installation supports Windows/Linux x64; Docker also needs device access and persistent state directory. This driver handles prepared persistent values: no inclusion, exclusion, SmartStart, reset, controller administration or Engineering discovery.

sections.heading: Source and address interpretation
sections.body: S0/S2 references are optional in source format, but secure devices need material matching the network. RF region and NVM identity belong to the host resource. New UI binding authoring is pending: the descriptor without extra fields does not produce the binding required by Runtime.

fields.label: Host controller resource
fields.description: ID of an available serial ZWaveController resource with RF region and network NVM identity registered by the administrator. Do not enter a serial path or RF parameters in this source. Region/identity must match the prepared controller.

fields.label: S0 Legacy key reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the host for this network. The administrator supplies the reference/slot; do not paste the secret key or put it in an Engineering package. Do not replace an existing key with a new value to troubleshoot connectivity.

fields.label: S2 Access Control key reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the host for this network. The administrator supplies the reference/slot; do not paste the secret key or put it in an Engineering package. Do not replace an existing key with a new value to troubleshoot connectivity.

fields.label: S2 Authenticated key reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the host for this network. The administrator supplies the reference/slot; do not paste the secret key or put it in an Engineering package. Do not replace an existing key with a new value to troubleshoot connectivity.

fields.label: S2 Unauthenticated key reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the host for this network. The administrator supplies the reference/slot; do not paste the secret key or put it in an Engineering package. Do not replace an existing key with a new value to troubleshoot connectivity.

fields.label: Persistent value address
fields.description: Identifies node, endpoint, Command Class, property and optional key, preserving string/number type. Not the operator display name. Must match the prepared controller inventory.

fields.label: Node
fields.description: Device number assigned by the existing Z-Wave network; not an IP address. Exclusion/reinclusion can require binding review.

fields.label: Endpoint
fields.description: Value endpoint on the device, including 0 for a root-node value. Not a serial/TCP port.

fields.label: Command Class
fields.description: Code of the class containing the value. Example 37 is Switch Binary; the driver admits bounded persistent values and rejects classes outside its scope. Not an Authority permission.

fields.label: Property and its type
fields.description: Use string/currentValue for the sample textual property. number/1 and string/1 properties have different identities; do not remove the type. Do not assume currentValue is writable.

fields.label: Optional key and its type
fields.description: key/none/- means no additional key. Where one exists keep its number/string type and escaped address contents; do not omit format components.

fields.label: Authoring a new binding
fields.description: This driver requires a versioned communication binding as well as Address. The generic assistant does not create a new binding when the descriptor has no extra fields, as here. Entering only a new TAG address is insufficient; authoring correction is pending. An existing valid binding received through package/API is a separate case.

sections.heading: Example: read binary switch state
sections.body: The example is a Boolean currentValue read from node 5. Use the installation’s actual values. The property may not be writable; commands require a controller-advertised writable value plus SCADIVO authorization. This is not an import package.

sections.heading: Verification and common failures
sections.body: Admitted TAG types are Boolean, Int16/Int32/Int64, Float/Double and String within accepted persistent properties. Check resource, region, NVM identity and security material, then complete address and actual value metadata. Missing values, incompatible types or unadvertised writes are not fixed by removing validation. Transient events do not automatically become persistent TAGs. Check feedback before treating a command as complete.

en.title: Zigbee2MQTT Bridge: inventory, selection and freshness
en.summary: Connect to an external installation and distinguish inventory, incorporation and fresh reports.

sections.heading: External installation and available workflow
sections.body:
Zigbee2MQTT and broker are managed outside SCADIVO. Devices must already be commissioned on the external network; this connector does not open inclusion, administer the coordinator or replace the Native Zigbee driver. Connection test, discovery and read test are advertised, but discovery without selection lists inventory only. The current UI does not send selection required for incorporation; that workflow awaits correction.

The external format puts exposes in definition.exposes; this parser version looks for exposes at the root. A device can therefore be listed without producing TAGs. Compatibility correction is pending separately from UI selection.

sections.heading: Source fields
sections.body: Host, base topic and credentials must match the broker actually used by the installation. Check connectivity from SCADIVO server, not only the browser.

fields.label: MQTT broker host
fields.description: Name/IP of the broker used by the external Zigbee2MQTT installation, reachable from SCADIVO server. Not the Zigbee2MQTT UI URL or a topic.

fields.label: Broker port
fields.description: Actual broker port. The form defaults to 1883; with TLS check its corresponding port rather than assuming automatic switching.

fields.label: Use TLS
fields.description: Enables protected transport where offered by the broker. Does not install certificates or replace broker authentication.

fields.label: Base topic
fields.description: Prefix configured on external Zigbee2MQTT. The driver uses, for example, baseTopic/bridge/state and baseTopic/bridge/devices. Do not put a device friendly name here.

fields.label: MQTT client ID
fields.description: Optional; empty generates a stable ID from source identity. If set, do not reuse the same ID on another active client. Not a user name or password.

fields.label: MQTT version
fields.description: mqtt5 or mqtt311 as supported by the broker. The driver uses its own session defaults; do not copy every MQTT Raw advanced setting into this source.

fields.label: Broker user
fields.description: Account permitted on the external installation topics. Separate from SCADIVO login.

fields.label: Broker password reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the host for this network. The administrator supplies the reference/slot; do not paste the secret key or put it in an Engineering package. Do not replace an existing key with a new value to troubleshoot connectivity.

fields.label: Keep Alive (s)
fields.description: Broker connection supervision. Does not request sensor measurements or wake a battery device.

fields.label: Connection timeout (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for connecting to the broker, separate from request or write-confirmation time.

fields.label: Request timeout (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for a query operation. Not a polling interval for every sensor.

fields.label: Write confirmation wait (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for a matching sufficiently fresh state report after a command. MQTT acceptance without feedback does not confirm equipment state.

fields.label: Minimum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Initial wait after connection loss. Reducing it does not repair an offline broker or rejected authentication.

fields.label: Maximum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Caps increasing wait and must be greater than or equal to minimum.

fields.label: Maximum message size (bytes)
fields.description: Limits received payload including inventories; increase only if actual documents require it and resources allow. Not history capacity.

fields.label: Connection failure limit
fields.description: Consecutive failure limit used by readiness supervision. Does not grant operation with an unreachable source.

fields.label: Maximum queued messages
fields.description: Limits the transport buffer. More messages use more memory; not persistent storage.

fields.label: Maximum inventory devices
fields.description: Inventory/selection limit for this source. Not a radio-capacity promise and does not remove license quotas.

fields.label: Maximum exposes per device
fields.description: Limits property descriptions processed per device. An expose is a function/property advertised by Zigbee2MQTT, not an automatically incorporated TAG.

sections.heading: Generated bindings and pending selection
sections.body: Technical fields below are produced by incorporation from selection/inventory. They are not IDs for the developer to invent. Until the page sends selection, listing a device does not guarantee ready Equipment/TAGs. Mapped scalar exposes are binary and numeric; functional capabilities depend on supported properties.

fields.label: IEEE, endpoint and property
fields.description: Stable address generated from IEEE, optional endpoint and property. Friendly name can change and must not become binding identity.

fields.label: Internal source identity — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Links to the saved source stable ID. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Source key — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Links to the readable source key. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: IEEE — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Normalized IEEE of the selected device, not friendly name. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Endpoint — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Endpoint advertised by the expose; may be absent. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Property — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Advertised property name such as temperature or state. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Expose type — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. binary produces Boolean TAG; numeric produces Double TAG. Other types do not become scalar TAGs through this workflow. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Advertised access — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Combinable bits: 1 state, 2 write, 4 request read. Must include 1; 5 means state plus request read. Does not grant security authorization. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Unit — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Must match the TAG unit; not an arbitrary scale conversion. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Minimum — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Advertised numeric lower bound, where supplied. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Maximum — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Advertised numeric upper bound, where supplied. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Step — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Positive numeric step where advertised; not read frequency. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: On value — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Explicit JSON value for true on a binary expose. Text ON and Boolean true have different types. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Off value — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Explicit JSON value distinct from the on value for a binary expose. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Point identity — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Combines source, IEEE, endpoint and property; copying from another source is invalid. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Equipment function — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. For example Temperature or OnOff; not a security capability granted to a user. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Confirmation contract — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Where supported requires matching non-retained state after the command with source freshness evidence. Not proof of physical actuation. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Explicit incorporation selection
fields.description: The service accepts IEEE selection, but the current Home/Building page does not send it. Without selection discovery lists inventory without incorporation content; selecting a row does not reissue the request with IEEE. UI incorporation awaits correction.

fields.label: Inventory format — current limitation
fields.description: The external format puts exposes in definition.exposes; this parser version looks for exposes at the root. A device can therefore be listed without producing TAGs. Compatibility correction is pending separately from UI selection.

sections.heading: Advertised inventory example
sections.body: The example below preserves the external format. The current parser does not extract its exposes; it demonstrates the limitation, not a completed import. Do not rewrite broker messages as an operational workaround.

sections.heading: State and quality example
sections.body: A retained message is Stale in this connector. Without source last_seen newer than the connection/bridge epoch, a report can be Uncertain even with retain false. Operation confirmation must also be newer than dispatch. Configure measurement information on the external installation and check times; receiving now does not prove measurement now. The sample instant is illustrative: use a current measurement for live tests.

sections.heading: Troubleshoot by layer
sections.body: No connection: check host/port/TLS/authentication. Connected without inventory: check baseTopic and bridge/state/devices. Inventory without incorporation: check the UI selection limit rather than recreating the network. Uncertain/Stale values: check retention, last_seen and reconnection. Unconfirmed write: check advertised access, confirmation binding, availability and fresh report; do not confirm a TAG just because the broker accepted publication.

en.title: Siemens S7: CPU, memory and first reading
en.summary: Configure ISO-on-TCP while distinguishing connection, DB access and write permission.

sections.heading: Prepare the PLC side
sections.body: Use the correct CPU and PLC project. This driver accesses absolute memory through S7 ISO-on-TCP; it is neither OPC UA nor full TIA symbolic browsing. For S7-1200/1500, have the PLC owner check permitted external access, PUT/GET where required and an absolute-compatible DB layout without optimization changing expected offsets. SCADIVO does not change these settings or replace installation protection.

sections.heading: Data Source fields
sections.body: Choose RackSlot or explicit TSAP to match the installation. A connection test negotiates a session; DB and individual point access still require verification.

fields.label: PLC address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. This is neither the browser address nor the project address.

fields.label: TCP port
fields.description: Port of the enabled PLC or adapter service. This driver defaults to 102. Check the firewall and actual service before changing it.

fields.label: CPU family
fields.description: Select S7300, S7400, S71200 or S71500 to match the installed CPU. Unknown does not define an operational profile. This does not enable PLC services or permissions automatically.

fields.label: How to locate the connection
fields.description: RackSlot derives the destination from rack, slot and role. ExplicitTsap uses the destination TSAP from the installation configuration. Choose one mode and fill its corresponding fields.

fields.label: Rack
fields.description: In RackSlot mode, the rack containing the CPU. This is not a project equipment number.

fields.label: CPU slot
fields.description: In RackSlot mode, actual CPU position. Example 1 does not fit every family; check the configured hardware.

fields.label: Connection role
fields.description: In RackSlot: OperatorPanel, ProgrammingDevice or Basic, matching the PLC connection. This is not an Authority user role.

fields.label: Enable Data Source writes
fields.description: Defaults to false. Writes also require a writable binding, non-ReadOnly TAG, writable destination and permission. This does not enable PUT/GET or change CPU protection.

fields.label: Source TSAP
fields.description: Client-side identifier in the ISO session. Default 0x0100. This is not a TCP port; keep the communication configuration value.

fields.label: Destination TSAP
fields.description: Required in ExplicitTsap mode. Use the identifier configured for the PLC connection; check it before copying the example.

fields.label: Connection timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed to establish the connection.

fields.label: Response timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed for a request response. Increasing this does not fix an incorrect address, route or type.

fields.label: Reconnect delay
fields.description: Milliseconds before retrying a failed connection. This is not the measurement interval; zero does not fix access denial.

fields.label: Requested message size
fields.description: PDU bytes requested during S7 negotiation. Default 480; accepted size depends on the PLC. This is neither the TAG count nor database size.

sections.heading: TAG binding fields
sections.body: The SCADIVO TAG path identifies the application variable; area, DB, byte and bit locate PLC memory. Portable address and binding fields must agree.

fields.label: Memory area
fields.description: Input: inputs; Output: outputs; Merker: M memory; DataBlock: DB. Match the actual program address. Reading inputs does not make that area writable.

fields.label: DB number
fields.description: For DataBlock, nonzero block number. Outside this area use zero. The number is not a byte offset.
fields.constraints: 1–65535 for DB; zero in other areas.

fields.label: Starting byte offset
fields.description: Zero-based position within the area/DB. DB1.DBD0 starts at byte 0; Float32 occupies four bytes. Do not enter 32 by confusing bits with bytes.

fields.label: Boolean bit
fields.description: Only Boolean uses bit 0–7 within the byte. Keep zero for other types; do not replace this field with the generic bit selector.

fields.label: Physical PLC type
fields.description: Choose actual storage: Boolean, Byte, SInt, UInt16, Int16, UInt32, Int32, Int64, Float32, Float64, String, WString, Date or DateTime. Float32 maps to TAG Float, Float64 to Double, text to String, dates to DateTime. A TAG name does not convert memory contents.

fields.label: Text capacity
fields.description: String/WString only: declared capacity of 1–254 characters; this is not numeric read size. Use zero for other types. Allow actual DB space for the format header.

fields.label: Allow writes to this point
fields.description: Start with false while checking reads. true only enables a point that is also writable in memory/protocol; TAG ReadOnly, session permissions and other restrictions still apply.

fields.label: Byte and word order
fields.description: The descriptor still declares Normal, ByteSwap, WordSwap and ByteAndWordSwap, but the current binding does not accept this setting or order in the address. Ordering is represented by the shared physical byte/word transform. This mismatch is part of the pending authoring correction; do not copy the catalog field into the binding as a manual solution.

fields.label: Binding authoring in this version
fields.description: The current catalog gives the generic assistant a binding identity different from the one required by the S7 Runtime. Creation through this path is rejected and awaits correction. Other fields and the example describe the correct S7 binding, not an already corrected authoring flow. Do not change internal IDs to bypass validation. The valueOrder field must also be projected to the physical transform rather than saved as an extra setting.

sections.heading: From Data Source to a checked reading
sections.body: Manual creation through the current assistant encounters the binding limitation described above. The example demonstrates valid binding parameters for review; it does not instruct you to force an internal identity in the UI. For a project with an already valid S7 binding, verify the source, a known reading and quality after publishing/activating through the project workflow. A successful connection test does not establish tested reads or writes.

sections.heading: Example: REAL at the start of DB1
sections.body: Configuration example, not a complete package. The PLC program must actually store a REAL at DB1.DBD0. Expected result is a Float reading of that value with writes disabled, not a test value generated by the driver.

sections.heading: TIA import and diagnosis
sections.body: Advertised import accepts compatible PLC TAG exports in XLSX, XML and SDF; this is not a full TIA project import or TIA Openness. Review candidates, types and addresses before applying. No connection: check IP, port 102, mode, rack/slot/TSAP and permitted access. Connected without readings: check DB number, absolute layout, offset and size. Implausible value: compare type, bytes and order with the program. Rejected write: check writeEnabled, writable, ReadOnly and permission; do not relax PLC protection as a test.

en.title: Allen-Bradley Logix: routing, symbols and reads
en.summary: Use ControlLogix/CompactLogix symbolic access and check limits before importing or writing.

sections.heading: Which connection you are configuring
sections.body: This driver uses explicit EtherNet/IP messages for ControlLogix/CompactLogix symbols. It is not cyclic I/O scanning for every EtherNet/IP device or a generic SLC/PLC-5/MicroLogix driver. Obtain the IP, profile, actual route and symbol external-access settings.

sections.heading: Data Source fields
sections.body: A CIP route differs from the TCP port. Identifying the controller proves neither a symbol read nor a write.

fields.label: PLC address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. This is neither the browser address nor the project address.

fields.label: TCP port
fields.description: Port of the enabled PLC or adapter service. This driver defaults to 44818. Check the firewall and actual service before changing it.

fields.label: Controller profile
fields.description: ControlLogix or CompactLogix to match the equipment. The profile does not automatically discover a slot or configure the PLC.

fields.label: CIP route to the CPU
fields.description: Ordered port,link hops separated by /. 1,0 represents a particular hop, not TCP port 1. Use the documented route; a direct destination may use an empty route according to profile. Do not guess additional hops.

fields.label: Read interval
fields.description: Requested milliseconds between acquisition cycles. 1000 means approximately one cycle per second, subject to network and processing time. This does not guarantee the PLC program update rate.

fields.label: Response timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed for a request response. Increasing this does not fix an incorrect address, route or type.

fields.label: Minimum reconnect delay
fields.description: Initial wait after a connection failure, in milliseconds. Must not exceed the maximum delay.

fields.label: Maximum reconnect delay
fields.description: Upper bound for progressive reconnect delay, in milliseconds. This is neither data validity nor command confirmation time.

fields.label: Points per batch
fields.description: Limits request grouping. Default 16; increasing it can raise load and message size. It does not change the licensed TAG count.

fields.label: Transport security requirement
fields.description: Unsecured is the available implementation. CipSecurityRequired is an explicit requirement rejected by this version; it neither enables CIP Security nor silently downgrades. If the installation requires CIP Security, this path does not meet that requirement.

sections.heading: Symbol binding fields
sections.body: Identity includes scope, program where applicable, path and native type. Do not copy a portable address while leaving fields aimed at a different symbol. Bool is readable; native Bool writing is not enabled in this version.

fields.label: Symbol scope
fields.description: Controller for a global symbol; Program for a program-local symbol with programName. This is not an Authority authorization scope.

fields.label: PLC program
fields.description: For Program scope, enter the actual program name. This is neither the SCADIVO application name nor the routine name.

fields.label: Symbol path
fields.description: Actual name and supported path, including member/index where applicable. Example TankLevel must exist in the PLC as REAL. Renaming the SCADIVO TAG does not rename the symbol.

fields.label: Native symbol type
fields.description: Runtime reads in this version: Bool, Sint, Int, Dint, Lint and Real, mapping to Boolean, Int16, Int16, Int32, Int64 and Float. Lreal/String may appear in the catalog/import but are not enabled for Runtime reading. Whole structures are not scalars.

fields.label: External access defined in the PLC
fields.description: ReadOnly permits reading; ReadWrite also permits compatible writing; None blocks access. Unknown does not prove write permission. This field describes the symbol; it does not change the PLC setting.

fields.label: Constant symbol
fields.description: true identifies a PLC constant and prevents writing. Do not use false to try making a constant writable.

fields.label: Physical integer bit
fields.description: Optional Boolean projection from Sint/Int/Dint/Lint: maximum indices 7/15/31/63. Not applicable to Real or Bool. It does not turn a write into a safe bit operation; check support before issuing commands. An accepted binding uses the shared physical selector, not an extra bitIndex setting; assistant projection is also pending.

fields.label: Binding authoring in this version
fields.description: Runtime stores symbolic identity in the portable address and requires empty extra settings. The current generic assistant copies the fields in this table into extra settings and its binding is rejected. Creation through this path awaits correction; the example shows a valid point contract, not a corrected assistant.

sections.heading: From Data Source to a checked reading
sections.body: Manual creation through the current assistant encounters the binding limitation described above. The example shows a valid read identity for review. For a project with an already valid Logix binding, verify source, symbol, type and quality after publishing/activating. Advertised Browse/import/reconciliation services require candidate and binding review before applying; opening a file does not establish a successful import.

sections.heading: Example: read-only REAL symbol
sections.body: TankLevel must exist at Controller scope as REAL. Use a Float, ReadOnly TAG for the first check. The example does not configure a rack route for you.

sections.heading: Browse, import and reconciliation
sections.body: Online Browse enumerates Controller-level symbols with pagination; it does not promise full program browsing. Compatible L5X/L5K import can include program scope. Review supported candidates, arrays, members and External Access; a visible symbol can be incompatible. Reconcile compares identities; it does not automatically modify the PLC program. For connection failure check IP/44818 and route. For missing symbols check scope, program and name. For rejected writes check supported type, constant, External Access, ReadOnly and permission.

en.title: Mitsubishi MELSEC: profile, routing and devices
en.summary: Configure MC/SLMP and check numeric radix, value width and CPU limits.

sections.heading: Prepare the MC service
sections.body: Have a compatible MC/SLMP TCP service and port enabled in the PLC. This profile uses binary 3E frames; it does not assume every model, ASCII, UDP or all Mitsubishi memory is supported. A familiar driver name does not replace the equipment profile.

sections.heading: Data Source fields
sections.body: Start with basic fields. Advanced routing and grouping must match the installation; defaults do not discover the topology automatically.

fields.label: PLC address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. This is neither the browser address nor the project address.

fields.label: TCP port
fields.description: Port of the enabled PLC or adapter service. This driver defaults to 5007. Check the firewall and actual service before changing it.

fields.label: Mitsubishi family profile
fields.description: Fx5U32MtDs or IqR04EnCpu: specific memory limits, not certification of all MELSEC CPUs. If the model differs, check compatibility before use.

fields.label: Read interval
fields.description: Requested milliseconds between acquisition cycles. 1000 means approximately one cycle per second, subject to network and processing time. This does not guarantee the PLC program update rate.

fields.label: Connection timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed to establish the connection.

fields.label: Response timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed for a request response. Increasing this does not fix an incorrect address, route or type.

fields.label: MC monitoring timer
fields.description: Time requested in the MC frame, in 250 ms units. Default 20 equals 5 s. This differs from the local response timeout, which must allow for that time and the network.

fields.label: MC network number
fields.description: Installation MC routing; default 0 for the directly configured destination. This is not the computer Ethernet-interface number.

fields.label: MC destination station
fields.description: Frame station field. Default 255 (FF). Use the MC route value, not a Modbus Unit ID.

fields.label: Module I/O number
fields.description: Hexadecimal routing field, default 03FF. This is not an output Y address; preserve the installation value.

fields.label: Multidrop station
fields.description: Additional MC routing field; default 0. Match the actual route without confusing it with IP or the frame station.

fields.label: Words per request
fields.description: Word grouping limit, default 64. A 32-bit value occupies two words; do not confuse words with TAG count.

fields.label: Bits per request
fields.description: Bit-device read limit, default 64. Adjust according to PLC capacity and measured load.

fields.label: Sparse points per request
fields.description: Limits grouping of noncontiguous addresses, default 16. It neither creates missing addresses nor changes the memory map.

fields.label: Blocks per request
fields.description: Limits grouped blocks, default 8. More blocks do not guarantee faster reads on saturated networks or CPUs.

fields.label: Explicit R address limit
fields.description: Optional. With no value, R is disabled. Enter the maximum validated for the installed memory; the current parser still caps R at 32767. The broad field maximum does not increase that profile limit.

sections.heading: Memory and binding fields
sections.body: Bit and word devices use different storage. Check this driver’s format even if another application writes the address differently.

fields.label: Device address
fields.description: X/Y/B/W use hexadecimal numbers; M/L/D/R use decimal. D100 is a decimal word address; X10 is hexadecimal 10, not another application’s octal convention. The profile limits the allowed range.

fields.label: Physical type
fields.description: Bit for bit areas; Int16, UInt16, Int32, UInt32 or Float32 for word areas. Int32/UInt32/Float32 occupy two consecutive words. Choose a compatible TAG and preserve PLC order; UInt32 uses TAG Int64. In SCADIVO, physical Int16/UInt16 use TAG Int32; physical Int32/UInt32 use Int64; Float32 uses Float; Bit uses Boolean.

fields.label: Allow writes to this point
fields.description: Start with false while checking reads. true only enables a point that is also writable in memory/protocol; TAG ReadOnly, session permissions and other restrictions still apply.

sections.heading: From Data Source to a checked reading
sections.body:
1. In Engineering > Data Sources, create the appropriate source and enter installation parameters.
2. Save and use Test connection when available. A successful connection does not prove all points.
3. In TAGs, select this source, choose a compatible type and fill the address and binding through the assistant. For manual authoring, address and fields must describe the same point; examples are not complete import packages.
4. Check a known reading using the point test when available, or after publishing/activating through the project workflow. Inspect value, quality and update in TAG Monitor.
5. Then configure a screen, alarm or authorized write. Compare the result with the PLC program and actual equipment condition.

sections.heading: Example: integer at D100
sections.body: D100 must contain a signed 16-bit integer in the PLC. Value 123 should appear as 123 in the Int32 TAG; check the raw value before applying unit conversion.

sections.heading: Targeted diagnosis
sections.body: No connection: check TCP service, port and MC routing. Invalid address: check area, decimal/hexadecimal and family limit; R needs an explicit limit. Misinterpreted value: check type and occupied words. Slow requests: compare the 250 ms MC timer units, local timeout, batches and load; do not increase everything together. A point test is not full Browse and does not certify writes or physical actuation.

en.title: Panasonic MEWTOCOL: TCP or serial and memory map
en.summary: Choose the actual transport and interpret words and contacts without mixing other protocols.

sections.heading: Choose profile and transport
sections.body: MEWTOCOL-COM TCP accesses a compatible TCP service or adapter; Host Serial uses the physical port visible on the server. These are distinct Data Sources. For serial, check cabling, RS-232/RS-485 and line settings. The driver does not turn a generic Ethernet converter into a server for every Panasonic protocol.

sections.heading: Source and binding fields
sections.body: For TCP fill host/port/connection timeout; for serial fill the port and line framing. Station, family, frame mode and acquisition apply to both. The final three fields describe the point.

fields.label: PLC address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. This is neither the browser address nor the project address.

fields.label: Adapter TCP port
fields.description: Required for TCP, with no assumed default port. Use the PLC/adapter MEWTOCOL-COM port; do not copy the Mitsubishi MC port.

fields.label: Connection timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed to establish the connection.

fields.label: Server serial port
fields.description: Host Serial only: device accessible to the SCADIVO service, such as COM4 on Windows or /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux. In Docker, device access and permissions belong to the container/host, not the browser.

fields.label: Serial speed
fields.description: Serial only: bits per second matching the PLC. Default 9600; this is not the read interval.

fields.label: Data bits
fields.description: Serial only: 7 or 8 to match the installation. Default 8. Together with parity and stop bits this defines serial framing.

fields.label: Parity
fields.description: Serial only: None, Odd or Even, matching the PLC. Default None. Incorrect parity can produce a timeout without an intelligible response.

fields.label: Stop bits
fields.description: Serial only: One or Two to match the PLC. Default One; do not use another driver’s values outside this list.

fields.label: Turnaround delay
fields.description: Serial only: pause in milliseconds for the line/adapter after a transaction. Default 0; adjust to actual needs, not to fix an incorrect station.

fields.label: MEWTOCOL station
fields.description: Configured PLC station, required from 1 to 99. This is neither rack slot, IP nor a Unit ID inherited from another protocol.

fields.label: Panasonic family profile
fields.description: Fp0rF32, FpXhCommon or Fp7RClassicCom. Each limits areas, addresses and writes. FP7 here is the classic COM subset, not all FP7 memory/features.

fields.label: Frame mode
fields.description: Standard is the default. Expanded increases capacity only in profiles that permit it; Fp0rF32 rejects it. It neither enables MEWTOCOL7 nor extends memory areas.

fields.label: Read interval
fields.description: Requested milliseconds between acquisition cycles. 1000 means approximately one cycle per second, subject to network and processing time. This does not guarantee the PLC program update rate.

fields.label: Response timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed for a request response. Increasing this does not fix an incorrect address, route or type.

fields.label: Panasonic address
fields.description: Use an area and number admitted by the profile: contacts X/Y/R/L/T/C or words WX/WY/WR/WL/DT/LD. DT100 is a decimal word; for X/Y/R/L contacts the final digit is hexadecimal bit 0–F within a decimal group. Do not reinterpret the entire address as hexadecimal.

fields.label: Physical type
fields.description: Boolean for a contact; UInt16 or Int16 for a word, with matching TAG type. This driver does not expose a 32-bit REAL or string as though it were one 16-bit word. In this driver both physical Int16 and UInt16 use TAG Int32. Boolean uses TAG Boolean.

fields.label: Allow writes to this point
fields.description: Start with false while checking reads. true only enables a point that is also writable in memory/protocol; TAG ReadOnly, session permissions and other restrictions still apply.

sections.heading: From Data Source to a checked reading
sections.body:
1. In Engineering > Data Sources, create the appropriate source and enter installation parameters.
2. Save and use Test connection when available. A successful connection does not prove all points.
3. In TAGs, select this source, choose a compatible type and fill the address and binding through the assistant. For manual authoring, address and fields must describe the same point; examples are not complete import packages.
4. Check a known reading using the point test when available, or after publishing/activating through the project workflow. Inspect value, quality and update in TAG Monitor.
5. Then configure a screen, alarm or authorized write. Compare the result with the PLC program and actual equipment condition.

sections.heading: Example: DT100 word over TCP
sections.body: Port 9094 is only an example of a configured adapter, not a universal Panasonic default. DT100 must contain a signed 16-bit integer; the Int32 TAG should display the same number. For Host Serial replace network fields with installation serial settings.

sections.heading: Diagnose without guessing memory-map changes
sections.body: No TCP response: check service port and station. No serial response: check server device access, wiring, baud/parity/stop bits and station. Address error: compare area and profile limit, including the contact digit. Incorrect value: check Int16 versus UInt16 and word versus contact. Writes rejected in X/T/C or another protected area cannot be resolved just by changing ReadOnly. Connection and point tests do not prove all memory or physical actuation.

es.title: Plantillas: crear un faceplate reutilizable
es.summary: Dibuje una vez y comprenda cómo los cambios llegan a equipos vinculados.

sections.heading: Comprenda qué está creando
sections.body: Una Plantilla Faceplate es una definición gráfica compartida, como una bomba con nombre, estado y lectura. Equipo identifica una bomba concreta. Bomba 01 y Bomba 02 pueden usar la misma plantilla; un equipo también puede existir sin ella. Un perfil de Intelligence organiza mediciones y no sustituye al dibujo.

sections.heading: Dónde entrar y qué rellenar
sections.body: Abra Ingeniería > Plantillas. El editor usa los mismos objetos, Propiedades, Dinámicas y Eventos que Pantallas. Necesita permiso de edición y bloqueo cuando se solicite.

fields.label: Nombre de plantilla
fields.description: Nombre legible en biblioteca. Describa su finalidad, no una instancia física.

fields.label: Identificador
fields.description: Referencia estable de los vínculos. Consérvela al actualizar el dibujo; cambiar el nombre visible no exige otro equipo.

fields.label: Objetos y vínculos
fields.description: Composición gráfica. Una referencia TAG fija sigue apuntando al mismo TAG al reutilizarse. Revise referencias de cada instancia antes de representar otro equipo.

sections.heading: Procedimiento: crear y reutilizar
sections.body: 1. Seleccione Nueva plantilla y complete nombre e identificador. 2. Inserte un conjunto pequeño y configure propiedades. 3. Añada vínculos/dinámicas/eventos; no suponga sustitución automática de TAGs por nombre de equipo. 4. Ejecute Preview, corrija errores y aplique. 5. Abra Equipos, cree o seleccione una instancia y elija esta plantilla opcional. Guarde el vínculo. 6. En Pantallas insértela desde la biblioteca de equipos/faceplates, cuando esté disponible. 7. Guarde, publique y active. Compruebe dos instancias y sus lecturas en Runtime.

sections.heading: Actualizar sin confundir definición e instancia
sections.body: Editar la plantilla compartida actualiza el dibujo de todas las instancias vinculadas en esa revisión. Revise el impacto; use otra plantilla si necesita apariencia distinta. Cambiar el vínculo cambia el dibujo asociado y conserva la identidad del equipo. Un Dínamo es otro conjunto visual reutilizable; un Grupo solo organiza objetos.

sections.heading: Si falta o no se actualiza
sections.body: Compruebe plantilla aplicada, vínculo correcto y revisión activa. Una copia independiente no se vincula por compartir nombre. Actualice y valide si cambió el proyecto. Si aparece la lectura de otra bomba, revise referencias y no solo el título.

es.title: Equipos: crear, identificar y asociar
es.summary: Registre el activo real y después elija su dibujo y mediciones.

sections.heading: Empiece por la identidad del activo
sections.body: Abra Ingeniería > Equipos. Equipo representa una instancia real, como Bomba 01. No es Driver, TAG ni dibujo. Puede crearlo sin faceplate y asociar plantilla después. Intelligence usa esta identidad; dibujar una bomba no registra el equipo.

sections.heading: Campos de instancia
sections.body: El formulario muestra nombre y plantilla opcional. El producto genera la ruta; no necesita inventarla ni escribirla.

fields.label: Nombre del equipo
fields.description: Rótulo para encontrar el activo. Distinga las instancias.

fields.label: Ruta generada
fields.description: Referencia estable para comprobar. Renombrar una instancia conserva su ruta. Una ruta generada duplicada impide crear otra.
fields.example: Compruebe la vista previa de ruta

fields.label: Plantilla Faceplate (opcional)
fields.description: Selecciona dibujo compartido. Sin plantilla es válido; quitar el vínculo no elimina equipo. Cambiarlo no elige TAGs ni perfiles de Intelligence automáticamente.

sections.heading: Procedimiento: registrar y comprobar
sections.body: 1. Introduzca un nombre distinto. 2. Compruebe ruta y elija plantilla o Sin plantilla. 3. Pulse Crear equipo; el producto valida antes de aplicar. 4. Selecciónelo en la lista para editar nombre/vínculo y guarde cambios. 5. Guarde/publique/active cuando se necesite en Runtime. 6. En Intelligence seleccione esta identidad y asigne perfil. Configure TAGs y captura antes de analizar.

sections.heading: Verificación y errores frecuentes
sections.body: La instancia debe aparecer con nombre, ruta y vínculo correcto. Sin plantilla no significa equipo inválido. Plantilla no disponible indica vínculo no resuelto: elija una existente o quite la asociación. Ruta duplicada requiere nombre distinto. Ante conflicto actualice y revise; no cree copias repetidas.

es.title: Base de datos: configurar, migrar y recuperar
es.summary: Comprenda la base activa antes de validar otro destino o migrar.

sections.heading: Dónde entrar y qué resuelve esta página
sections.body: Abra Ingeniería > Base de datos. Se requiere SystemAdmin. Local Managed usa almacenamiento local administrado; Remote usa PostgreSQL configurado. Esto elige almacenamiento, no redundancia HA. Lea Estado actual y Próxima acción. Un Local Managed saludable no necesita perfil Remote si satisface su instalación.

sections.heading: Prepare el destino
sections.body: Acuerde servidor, base, cuenta, certificados y permisos con el administrador. La dirección debe ser accesible por el servicio SCADIVO, no solo el navegador. En Docker localhost dentro del contenedor es ese contenedor. En Windows/Linux los certificados deben existir en el servidor del servicio. Haga backup y planifique mantenimiento.

sections.heading: Campos básicos y avanzados
sections.body: Empiece con host, usuario y secreto. Abra Configuración avanzada solo para cambiar valores propuestos. Los ejemplos son demostrativos, no credenciales.

fields.label: Host / FQDN
fields.description: DNS/dirección de PostgreSQL accesible al servicio, no la URL web.

fields.label: Usuario / identidad
fields.description: Cuenta PostgreSQL de aplicación; no su login de Authority SCADIVO.

fields.label: Contraseña / secreto
fields.description: Se envía sin devolverse en el estado. Limpiarse al enviar no significa perder credencial. No incluya en incidencias ni capturas.

fields.label: Database
fields.description: Nombre de base destino, no de proyecto. Inicialmente elitescada; confírmelo.

fields.label: Puerto
fields.description: Puerto PostgreSQL. Inicialmente 5432, distinto del HTTPS de aplicación.

fields.label: Modo TLS
fields.description: Require exige cifrado. VerifyCa valida cadena CA; VerifyFull también el nombre del servidor. Prefer y Disable no ofrecen igual protección. Use el modo acordado con TI; no desactive TLS para ocultar un error.
fields.example: Require o VerifyFull con CA válida

fields.label: Ruta del certificado CA
fields.description: Archivo CA legible por el servicio; exigido para VerifyCa/VerifyFull. Una ruta del equipo del navegador no sirve a otro host/contenedor.

fields.label: Timeout (s)
fields.description: Espera de conexión; inicialmente 15 segundos. Aumentarla no corrige usuario, DNS ni certificado.

fields.label: Historian usa Primary / dedicado
fields.description: Marcado, histórico usa base principal. Desmarque solo para destino Historian dedicado y complete su endpoint; también debe superar compatibilidad.

sections.heading: Migrar datos a otra base
sections.body: 1. Compruebe base activa y haga backup. 2. Complete Remote y Valide destino: conexión, autenticación, TLS y compatibilidad; accesibilidad no basta. 3. Prepare migración y revise origen, destino y datos. La configuración queda bloqueada. 4. En mantenimiento Inicie migración; escrituras durables pueden pausarse. 5. Espere copia y verificación automática. 6. Tras verificación correcta, Active banco Remote y confirme. 7. Si se exige reinicio, reinicie/reabra el servicio y compruebe topología, salud, proyecto y revisión antes de operar.

sections.heading: Conectar a base existente no es migrar
sections.body: Conectar a base existente (sin copia) no copia ni mezcla registros. Úselo solo con destino preparado del mismo proyecto y revisión activa exigidos. Lea confirmación. La incompatibilidad bloquea cambio; no vacíe ni modifique base para evitar comprobación. Para transportar datos actuales use migración.

sections.heading: Revertir y volver al banco local
sections.body: Si se exige Recovery/Rollback, revise diagnóstico y Revierta operación cuando esté disponible. Volver a Local Managed valida/reactiva almacenamiento local conservado y puede exigir reinicio. No mezcla automáticamente escrituras posteriores de Remote con el local. Conserva la base anterior; volver no restaura un backup ni elimina Remote. Compruebe datos y revisión activos.

sections.heading: Errores que requieren acciones diferentes
sections.body: Sin conexión: revise DNS/puerto/acceso del servicio. Autenticación rechazada: cuenta PostgreSQL/secreto. TLS: CA, nombre y validez. Incompatibilidad: versión PostgreSQL, capacidad TimescaleDB exigida y schema. Fase inválida: actualice y siga Próxima acción; no inicie otra copia. Almacenamiento indisponible puede degradar Runtime; memoria no debe simular persistencia. Para soporte registre hora, fase e ID sin contraseñas.

es.title: HA: configurar dos servidores y seguir la operación
es.summary: Distinga configuración guardada, servidor activo, compañero listo y protección contra ejecución duplicada.

sections.heading: Qué preparar primero
sections.body: HA significa Alta Disponibilidad: dos servidores pueden asumir Runtime de forma controlada. Abra Ingeniería > Alta disponibilidad. Requiere licencia HA Runtime y HighAvailabilityObserve; guardar/operar también HighAvailabilityTransfer. Compruebe red entre servicios, autenticación, relojes y almacenamiento de cada nodo. Bases compartidas o separadas necesitan comprobar topología; habilitar HA no crea replicación ni prueba disponibilidad.

sections.heading: Rellene solo lo que depende de la instalación
sections.body: La página distingue Este servidor y Servidor compañero. El operador no necesita inventar identidades internas ni transporte automático.

fields.label: Dirección principal de cada servidor
fields.description: Endpoint accesible entre servicios. La dirección detectada solo sirve si el compañero la alcanza; localhost en dos hosts no es un servidor.

fields.label: Dirección externa alternativa
fields.description: Abra solo si la red exige otra dirección anunciada. En otro caso conserve automática para evitar destinos inconsistentes.

fields.label: Servidor preferente
fields.description: Preferencia de inicio/failback; no fuerza promoción ni establece preparación.

fields.label: Autenticación entre servidores
fields.description: Configure secreto compartido mediante flujo protegido en ambos nodos. Se limpia del formulario; compruebe estado sin capturarlo.

fields.label: Protección y referencia compartida
fields.description: Fencing evita dos ejecutores Active. Ambos deben ver la misma referencia externa compartida; dos archivos locales con igual nombre no son autoridad compartida.

fields.label: Failover automático
fields.description: Permite cambio automático elegible y exige protección. No sustituye compañero preparado, datos disponibles ni seguridad.

sections.heading: Procedimiento de preparación
sections.body: 1. Compruebe modo En ejecución. 2. Prepare HA con dos direcciones y preferencia. 3. Configure autenticación/protección compartida y resuelva preparación. 4. Guarde configuración deseada; Guardado no equivale a En ejecución. 5. Si se exige, planifique reinicios y compruebe configuración cargada. 6. Actualice y revise Active efectivo, compañero, base y protección. Standby no equivale a Ready Standby. 7. Antes de operar haga ensayo manual acordado con responsable; las comprobaciones del manual no lo sustituyen.

sections.heading: Lea estados antes de operar
sections.body: Active efectivo está autorizado a ejecutar, no es solo preferido. Synchronizing aún recibe/verifica estado. Ready Standby indica preparación evaluada; Standby no la prueba. Promoting/Demoting son transiciones. Stale es observación antigua; Isolated, Faulted, degradación o autoridad ambigua exigen diagnóstico. Banco disponible difiere de compañero accesible. No oculte fallo de base aumentando tolerancias de red.

sections.heading: Elija la operación correcta
sections.body: Switchover transfiere de Active efectivo a compañero elegible. Failback solicita volver al preferente cuando se permite. Recovery reconcilia fallo/bloqueo. Forzar resincronización es recuperación específica sin Active y con autoridad anterior cercada; no declara listo a un compañero. Lea destino, confirmación y resultado; compruebe historial y Active resultante. No repita rechazo sin cambiar su causa.

sections.heading: Ajustes avanzados: significado y límites
sections.body: Parta de valores propuestos. Cambiar tiempos afecta protección y respuesta; evalúe red, relojes y operación. Los límites del formulario no son recomendaciones de rendimiento.

fields.label: Freshness (s)
fields.description: Edad máxima de observación reciente.

fields.label: Lease (s)
fields.description: Validez de autoridad de ejecución; no es licencia comercial.

fields.label: Poll (ms)
fields.description: Intervalo de consulta de referencia; menor aumenta frecuencia.

fields.label: Edad máxima de witness (s)
fields.description: Edad máxima de evidencia de compañero listo; no crea preparación.

fields.label: Margen de reloj (s)
fields.description: Margen por diferencia de relojes; no sustituye sincronización.

sections.heading: Si hay problemas
sections.body: 403: revise permisos. Guardado difiere de ejecución: reinicio pendiente. Compañero inaccesible: direcciones/red/autenticación. Referencia indisponible: almacenamiento externo compartido. Compañero no listo: sincronización/base/diagnóstico sin forzar promoción. Registre hora, acción, resultado y nodo efectivo; nunca secreto.

es.title: Intelligence: habilitar, pausar y resolver bloqueos
es.summary: Licencia disponible, recurso seleccionado y ejecución activa son condiciones diferentes.

sections.heading: Siga la secuencia completa
sections.body: Abra Ingeniería > Inteligencia de activos. Cree Equipo y TAGs, después perfiles, asociaciones Equipo/perfil, contextos y etapas útiles. Guarde configuración y alcances; publique/active revisión. Después active explícitamente el recurso para análisis. Crear perfil, marcar casilla o tener licencia no habilita ejecución automáticamente.

sections.heading: Permisos y selección de recursos
sections.body: EngineeringModify permite configurar; AssetProcessIntelligenceManage debe ser explícito, global o sobre Equipo/Ubicación. El nombre Developer o SystemAdmin por sí solo no sustituye ese permiso. Consultas también necesitan TrendUse y licencia Intelligence. Conceda en Seguridad y revise capacidades efectivas. Seleccione recursos sin memorizar IDs y conserve identidad.

sections.heading: Activar solo donde sea útil
sections.body: 1. Seleccione Equipos/Ubicaciones en Alcances elegibles. 2. Guarde alcances y configuración. 3. Publique/active y resuelva cambios pendientes. 4. Pulse Activar en el recurso y confirme permiso habilitado. 5. Abra consulta de asociación y elija período. 6. Pausar cancela trabajo pendiente sin eliminar TAGs/histórico. Pause antes de quitar un recurso de selección.

sections.heading: Activo configurado no significa habilitado
sections.body: Tras revocación, el permiso puede quedar cerrado aunque configuración siga activa. Restaurar permiso no rearma silenciosamente: revise y Active otra vez, también tras reinicio cuando se indique. Evita reiniciar análisis sin decisión del responsable. Distíngalo de errores Historian o falta de datos.

sections.heading: Ejemplo: empezar pequeño
sections.body: Empiece con Bomba 01 en un área. Configure corriente y velocidad si existen; no invente vibración. Añada mediciones/análisis admitidos por catálogo. Mantenga pausado lo no utilizado. La selección controla ejecución elegible, no promete consumo fijo de CPU/RAM.

es.title: Intelligence: significado de señales y unidades
es.summary: Describa qué se midió, no solo el nombre del TAG.

sections.heading: Por qué no basta el nombre
sections.body: Un TAG Potencia puede ser activa/aparente o calculada; presión puede ser aspiración, descarga o diferencial. Las reglas no deben adivinar por nombre. Seleccione papel semántico controlado requerido y complete calificadores mostrados. El papel legado es descriptivo.

sections.heading: Campos y elecciones
sections.body: Elija solo significado sustentado por instrumento y proceso. Los selectores muestran opciones del catálogo actual.

fields.label: Obligatorio
fields.description: Marca señales cuya ausencia compromete cobertura. No haga opcional una señal esencial solo para obtener resultado.

fields.label: Papel semántico
fields.description: Magnitud/función controlada; análisis usa ese papel, no semejanza de nombre.
fields.example: Potencia activa de entrada, si se mide

fields.label: Base de corriente
fields.description: Distingue base admitida, como corriente RMS apropiada; no deduzca de etiqueta genérica.

fields.label: Tipo de señal
fields.description: Distingue medición, referencia y función exigida. Una consigna no prueba valor medido.

fields.label: Referencia de presión
fields.description: Identifica base/origen; diferencial salida menos entrada difiere de solo descarga.

fields.label: Dirección del flujo
fields.description: Identifica sentido de transferencia; el opuesto puede invalidar regla.

fields.label: Referencia de frecuencia
fields.description: Explica frecuencia según catálogo; distinga referencia eléctrica y velocidad física.

fields.label: TAG y unidad
fields.description: Seleccione TAG real y unidad controlada. Cambiar rótulo no convierte datos. Algunos cálculos exigen unidades/versiones específicas.
fields.example: kW para potencia si corresponde al dato real

sections.heading: Ejemplo: no confundir indicador con eficiencia
sections.body: Corriente creciente a igual velocidad puede justificar investigación, pero no calcula eficiencia física. Potencia de entrada, caudal y diferencial pueden habilitar otras reglas con papeles/unidades/alineación adecuados. Si falta instrumento/calificador, lea motivo de indisponibilidad; no invente valores.

es.title: Intelligence: consultar resultados y crear dashboards
es.summary: Elija la pregunta, compruebe datos disponibles y después interprete el indicador.

sections.heading: Empiece por cobertura
sections.body: Con asociación guardada y ejecución autorizada, abra cobertura. Introduzca inicio/fin y consulte explícitamente. El formulario usa hora local y respuesta identifica ventana UTC; fin debe seguir inicio. Revise señales obligatorias, muestras aceptadas/rechazadas, calidad y alineación antes de mínimos/máximos/media. Contar muestras no prueba cadencia, completitud ni sincronización.

sections.heading: Rendimiento: elija regla elegible
sections.body: Abra Rendimiento y elija regla del catálogo. Opciones deshabilitadas explican señales/papeles/unidades ausentes. No elija otra magnitud solo para obtener número. Complete Desde/Hasta, consulte y revise estado/unidad/ventana/límites. Indisponible no es cero; un indicador no es eficiencia física. Cambiar asociación/revisión/parámetros exige nueva consulta.

sections.heading: Dos tipos de contexto con límites distintos
sections.body: Contextos operativos guardados usan límites numéricos inclusivos en unidad actual y evidencia del mismo timestamp UTC exacto de origen. El generador de pantalla de desviación usa selección distinta: 2–8 objetivos y dos contextos numéricos distintos entre sí y de objetivos; al menos cuatro señales utilizables. Sus rangos usan unidad controlada mostrada y límite inferior ≤ valor < superior. No copie automáticamente límites del perfil: unidad y extremo superior pueden diferir.

sections.heading: Genere pantalla y compruebe la cadena completa
sections.body: 1. Elija asociación/etapa y tipo de pantalla. 2. Complete selecciones y lea motivos si se bloquea. 3. Genere borrador: organiza objetos/referencias, no consulta Historian ni activa. 4. Revise nombre, dimensiones, objetos, vínculos y navegación; Preview y Apply. 5. Guarde/publique/active y abra en Runtime. 6. Configure/ejecute consulta y revise ventana/resultado. Una etapa agrupa miembros sin crear automáticamente KPI agregado ni probar causalidad.

sections.heading: Cómo investigar resultado vacío
sections.body: Compruebe en orden: licencia/permisos; alcance guardado/permiso habilitado; proyecto/revisión activa; asociación/TAGs; período; captura Historian; calidad; papeles/unidades; alineación/contexto. Corrija la primera carencia comprobada y consulte. No amplíe límites ni cambie significado solo para obtener resultado. El análisis apoya investigación; no confirma defectos ni predicción validada en campo.

es.title: Por dónde empezar en cada área
es.summary: Encuentre la tarea y siga las guías relacionadas al final.

sections.heading: Un orden para construir su aplicación
sections.body: Empiece con conexión de datos, compruebe TAGs, represente equipos, construya Pantallas/Popups, configure alarmas/histórico y después analice con Intelligence. Scripts añaden lógica. Seguridad, licencia, base y HA son administraciones distintas. La primera aplicación no requiere todas las funciones.

sections.heading: Proyecto y comunicación
